thought: the paste went on a prince; she could have sold it as royal
line: Ought to call it the prince's paste now. Sell twice as much, I would.

thought: running through the recipe, tickled it was fit for royalty
line: Ash, flour, water, redberries. Good enough for a prince, apparently.

thought: proud of how well the disguise worked
line: Mix a bit of ash in, and nobody knows a prince from a pauper.

thought: stirring and muttering; sure the muttering did it
line: The muttering's what does it. Worked on the prince, didn't it?

thought: wondering idly what became of her paste on the prince
line: Wonder if that prince ever washed my paste off. Shame if he did.

thought: off redberry picking again, a grievance despite the fame
line: A prince wore my paste, and still I'm picking my own redberries.

thought: marvelling at where her little potion ended up
line: A prince's face, and a witch's paste. Who'd have thought it?

thought: she makes pretty things; disguising was a new use
line: I make things pretty, mostly. Making a prince look ordinary was new.

thought: spots the player who carried her paste off for the rescue
line: There's my clever one. Got a prince out under a dab of paste!

thought: offers help for the next rescue, fond
line: Hello, dearie. Any more princes need hiding, you know where I am.

thought: remembers the player carried the paste carefully
line: You carried that paste so careful, dearie. Not a smear wasted.

thought: tells the cauldron about the player, witchy whimsy
line: Aggie told the cauldron all about that one. It bubbled, very pleased.

thought: credits the pair of them, mostly the paste
line: Fooled Lady Keli, the pair of us. Well, mostly my paste.

thought: a witch likes her work used well
line: A witch likes a customer who puts her paste to proper use, dearie.

thought: greets the player by a new pet name
line: Ooh, it's my prince-smuggler! Mind how you go, dearie.

thought: thinks the player understood what a disguise needs
line: You'd make a decent witch, my dear. You know what paste is for.

thought: never got thanked for the royal paste
line: Paste for a prince, and did I get a thank-you? Not from you, dearie.

thought: the paste did the real work, the player only carried it
line: Who got the prince out? My paste. You just carried the pot.

thought: one disguise doesn't make a witch
line: Don't think one disguised prince makes you a witch, dearie.

thought: busy rescuing princes but not saying hello
line: Rescuing princes, and you can't stop to say hello to a witch?

thought: Keli was fooled; Aggie isn't
line: Lady Keli was fooled by my paste, dearie. Aggie isn't fooled by you.

thought: expects the player back wanting paste for every scrape
line: Don't come asking for prince's paste for every scrape you're in.

thought: fame doesn't excuse the fine for rudeness
line: Saved a prince, did you? The fine for cheek is still the fine, dearie.

thought: the player never picked their own redberries
line: I'll bet you never picked a redberry for that paste yourself.

thought: Baba's reputation as a thief is, to Ali, the highest praise
line: Baba, called a thief for selling too well. I could weep with pride.

thought: all that business and the stall is still his alone
line: Still no assistant behind this counter. After all that, my friend!

thought: calls the scheme tourism, proudly
line: Tourism, my friend. Pollnivneach has never been so full of visitors.

thought: hunting new suppliers for the expansion
line: Suppliers! Who in this desert sells blackjacks by the crate?

thought: fond of his partners in Pollnivneach
line: The mayor and I understand each other. Men of business, both of us.

thought: the boy is in hiding, which Ali takes as a mark of talent
line: Hiding, the boy is. The best salesmen always have to hide a while.

thought: grand plans, only missing the goods
line: Expansion, my friend! Fine clothes, runes... I only need a supplier.

thought: his family spreading the trade everywhere
line: Farid at the Exchange, Baba in hiding. My family does get about.

thought: the player went all that way; he calls it tourism
line: My friend! You went all the way to Pollnivneach. A true tourist.

thought: offers a family price to the one who found Baba
line: For the one who found my Baba, a price I give only to family.

thought: would hire the player; the post is still open
line: Behind this counter, my friend, there is still room for one more.

thought: remembers the player bought the disguise without complaint
line: Ah, my best customer! A beard, a headdress, and never a complaint.

thought: the player found the boy where a whole town could not
line: You found the boy when a whole town could not. Remarkable, my friend.

thought: the greatest salesman pays a rare compliment
line: The greatest salesman in the world tips his hat to you, my friend.

thought: the player took the scheme in good part
line: Such a good sport, my friend! Not everyone enjoys a little tourism.

thought: Baba would approve of the player, a fellow seller
line: Baba would like you, my friend. You both know how to disappear.

thought: the player crossed the desert, and paid him for the privilege
line: You crossed the desert for my nephew? And you paid for the beard!

thought: the player was slow to see the business in it
line: Took you a while to see the business in it, my friend. Tourism!

thought: walks past a job and he still has no assistant
line: Still no assistant, and you walk past a perfectly good job, my friend.

thought: wouldn't let the player mind the stall, having seen them bargain
line: I would ask you to mind the stall, but I have seen you bargain.

thought: a tourist who complains disappoints the town
line: A tourist who complains? Pollnivneach would be so disappointed.

thought: the false beard went to the player's head
line: A false beard went to your head, my friend. It happens to tourists.

thought: the player fetched a nephew who needed no fetching
line: You fetched a nephew who did not need fetching. A born customer, you.

thought: offers another relative to find, a wink at the scheme
line: My favourite visitor! Would you care to find another relative?

thought: the dragon gone, he wonders whether Crandor will speak again
line: Crandor without its dragon. I wonder if word will come from it again.

thought: the roof lookouts are pointless now
line: I've had the roof swept. There's nothing up there to watch for now.

thought: the dragon-slayer keeps taking shields
line: Another shield gone to the dragon-slayer. I really must order more.

thought: likes to think his shield helped
line: Elvarg slain, with one of my shields. I like to think it helped.

thought: his father never slept for fear; he will
line: Father never slept a whole night for fear of that dragon. I shall.

thought: pleased his rule about worthy causes proved right
line: Shields for the worthy, I always said, and for once I was right.

thought: Lumbridge has something Varrock lacks
line: Lumbridge has a dragon-slayer now. Varrock has nothing of the sort.

thought: a quiet prayer of thanks, pompously phrased
line: Saradomin be thanked, there is one dragon fewer in the world.

thought: greets the dragon-slayer formally
line: Ah, the slayer of Elvarg! Lumbridge is honoured, my dear.

thought: the shield is theirs whenever they like
line: A shield whenever you like, adventurer. You've more than earned it.

thought: his father's fear is ended at last
line: Father would have given you the whole roof, I expect, for that dragon.

thought: relieved the player proved brave and not reckless
line: Brave and not reckless, after all. I did wonder, about the dragon.

thought: the worthy cause found a worthy bearer
line: That was a truly worthy cause, and you a most worthy bearer.

thought: amazed the dragon fell to someone who passes his door
line: To think Crandor's dragon fell to someone who walks past my door.

thought: fussing about receiving a dragon-slayer properly
line: Hmm, a dragon-slayer in my castle. I must have the good chairs dusted.

thought: the slayer of his father's dragon deserves a blessing
line: By Saradomin, the dragon my father feared is gone. I've you to thank.

thought: slew a dragon, still can't knock
line: Elvarg slain, and you still can't knock? Dragon-slayers, honestly.

thought: keeps coming back for shields
line: Another shield already? One begins to wonder what you do with them.

thought: the castle hears of the dragon daily
line: One dragon, and the castle hears of it daily. Do pace yourself.

thought: worries the player will lead the next dragon home
line: Do try not to lead the next dragon back here, my dear.

thought: father kept lookouts for the dragon; he'd keep one for the player
line: Father posted lookouts for a dragon. I may yet post one for you.

thought: heroics don't excuse muddy boots
line: Slaying dragons is all very well. Wiping one's boots would be better.

thought: his shields aren't for propping doors
line: Dragon-slayer or not, my shields are not for propping doors open.

thought: fusses over whether his shield survived
line: I gave you that shield in good faith. I trust it's still in one piece?

thought: the graveyard is quiet and he's forgotten what that's like
line: Quiet in the graveyard at last. I'd almost forgotten the sound of it.

thought: he used to say good night and get an answer; now nothing
line: Not a moan from the graveyard all week. I keep listening for one.

thought: visitors come to the graves again
line: People visit the graves again. Saradomin be praised for small mercies.

thought: still wary of warlocks after the skull business
line: Skull-stealing warlocks. I still lock the vestry, just in case.

thought: means to write to Urhney with the news
line: Must write to Urhney and tell him. He'll pretend not to care.

thought: holy water left over, nothing to use it on
line: Holy water left over, and no ghost to use it on. Waste not...

thought: swept the paths without looking over his shoulder
line: I swept the graveyard paths this morning without once looking round.

thought: likes to think his 'Avaunt' helped in the end
line: Avaunt worked in the end, I like to think. With a little help.

thought: recognises the one who laid the ghost
line: Ah, the one who laid our ghost to rest! Bless you, traveller.

thought: points the player out as the graveyard's friend
line: There goes the friend of our graveyard. The dead rest easier now.

thought: getting help from Urhney is its own miracle
line: A kind word out of Urhney and a ghost at rest. A miracle, nearly.

thought: keeps the player in his prayers, honestly
line: I mention you in my prayers, traveller. Most evenings, anyway.

thought: the graveyard looks better since
line: The graves look tidier since you came by. Saradomin's work, and yours.

thought: a warlock's mischief undone by a passer-by
line: A warlock's mischief, undone by a passer-by. Saradomin does provide.

thought: admits the player was braver than him
line: You were braver in that graveyard than I ever was, my friend.

thought: offers a blessing whenever wanted
line: If ever you need a blessing, traveller, you know where to find me.

thought: well done with the ghost; now the player's own soul
line: Good work with the ghost. Now, about your own soul...

thought: the player walks boldly past the graveyard now, unlike before
line: You walk past my graveyard so boldly now. It was not always so.

thought: one ghost doesn't make a priest
line: One ghost laid, and you think yourself a priest? It takes more prayer.

thought: no warlock-hunting in his pews
line: No warlock-hunting in my pews, traveller. They're for sitting.

thought: Saradomin saw the good deed and the missed services
line: Saradomin saw what you did for the ghost. He also sees an empty pew.

thought: hopes the player thanked Urhney; nobody ever does
line: I hope you thanked Urhney. Somebody ought to, once in his life.

thought: deflates the player: a ghost is only a lost parishioner
line: Don't look so pleased. A ghost is only a very lost parishioner.

thought: the player handled a stolen skull, which makes him squeamish
line: You carried that skull about by hand? I'd have used tongs.

thought: still can't believe the talk of penguins dressed as sheep
line: Penguins in my field, dressed as sheep. Whatever next?

thought: counted the flock and they're all sheep
line: Counted the flock again. Sheep, every last woolly one of 'em.

thought: sheep don't waddle; he knows his trade
line: Sheep don't waddle. I've farmed long enough to know that much.

thought: The Thing is bad enough without birds
line: The Thing's bad enough without folk adding penguins to it.

thought: imagines what nonsense comes next
line: Penguins on a sheep farm. Next it'll be fish in the onion bed.

thought: he'll worry when a sheep squawks
line: If one of my sheep starts squawking, then I'll worry. Not before.

thought: different folk see different things in a sheep
line: Some folk see a sheep and think birds. I see a sheep and think wool.

thought: the gate's open again; he refuses to blame birds
line: Gate's open again. And don't nobody tell me it was penguins.

thought: grudging: the player meant well
line: You meant well, with your penguins. I'll give you that much.

thought: odd, but shuts the gates
line: Odd sort, you, but you shut my gates. That counts for plenty.

thought: whatever the player saw, the sheep came to no harm
line: Whatever you saw out there, my sheep came to no harm. Much obliged.

thought: decent, even if they hear voices
line: Decent folk, you, even if you do hear voices about birds.

thought: a keen eye, too keen
line: Keen eyes, you've got. See things that aren't there, but keen.

thought: the player frets over his flock more than he does
line: You fret over my sheep more than I do. Wrong way round, but kind.

thought: at least someone watches his field
line: Least you were watching my field. Most folk just tramp through it.

thought: if anyone could spot The Thing, it's this one
line: You'd spot The Thing if anyone would. You spot everything, you do.

thought: sorry to report the sheep are still sheep
line: Back again? The sheep are still sheep, you'll be sorry to hear.

thought: penguins dressed as sheep, and they call him simple
line: Birds in sheep's wool, says you. And folk call farmers simple.

thought: send the bird talk to the chickens
line: Go and tell the chickens about your penguins. They might listen.

thought: Seth Groats has all the birds anyone could want
line: If you're wanting birds, try Seth Groats. He's got loads.

thought: it's sheep, they baa
line: Hearing voices in my field, are you? It's sheep. They baa.

thought: mock-asks which sheep is the spy
line: Which one's the penguin, then? The one looking at you funny?

thought: no poking his sheep for feathers
line: Don't you go poking my sheep for feathers, you scoundrel.

thought: points out the stranger who thinks his ewes have beaks
line: There goes the one who thinks my ewes have beaks.

thought: the prince is home; even the books look happier
line: The prince is home, and the ledgers have never looked so cheerful.

thought: the Emir rests easier, and so does he
line: The Emir rests easier now his son is home. So, I confess, do I.

thought: Osman won't say how it was done
line: Osman says nothing of how it was done. I have stopped asking.

thought: the palace is quiet in the good way again
line: We are a quiet palace again, and a quiet palace is a happy one.

thought: he writes the Emir's thanks for him now
line: I write the Emir's thanks for him now. He tires so very easily.

thought: still checks the prince's rooms out of habit
line: I find myself checking the prince's rooms each morning. Habit.

thought: someone has been at the windows; surely not the rescuer
line: Scrabbling at the windows again. Not our rescuer, I do hope.

thought: the city's true wealth is water, and now its prince too
line: We have water, and now we have our prince. A rich city indeed.

thought: greets the friend of Al Kharid
line: Ah, our friend of Al Kharid! The palace will never forget you.

thought: the Emir is too frail, so Hassan thanks the player for him
line: The Emir is too frail to say it himself, so I shall. Thank you.

thought: water for the rescuer, always
line: Water for you, whenever you wish. It is the least we can offer.

thought: good day on the Emir's behalf
line: On behalf of the Emir, good day to the one who brought his son home.

thought: the player did what a palace couldn't
line: You did what an entire palace could not. We remember such things.

thought: glad to see the rescuer in the streets
line: Our prince's rescuer, walking our streets. I do like to see it.

thought: knew the player could do it; Osman claims he knew first
line: I knew you could get the job done. Osman claims he knew first.

thought: the Emir's gratitude, and his own humbler share
line: Our Emir is forever grateful, and so, in my humbler way, am I.

thought: a friend, yes, but the window still isn't a door
line: A friend of Al Kharid, yes. The windows are still not a door.

thought: rescued the prince but still won't wipe their boots
line: You rescued the prince, and still you will not wipe your boots?

thought: gratitude has no limit, the treasury has
line: Our gratitude is boundless. Our treasury, I must remind you, is not.

thought: no statue for the hero
line: Do not expect a statue. We are a wealthy city, not a foolish one.

thought: welcome, though he'd still count the spoons
line: Welcome as ever, though I would still count the spoons after you.

thought: a rescue doesn't open the kitchens
line: Rescuing a prince does not entitle one to the palace kitchens.

thought: asks the hero to be less heroic indoors
line: Our hero returns. Do try to be a little less heroic indoors.

thought: grateful, truly, but no need to keep reminding them
line: We are grateful, truly. You need not remind us quite so often.

thought: one old recipe nearly killed everyone; back to burnt cakes
line: Nearly got everyone killed with one old recipe. I'll stick to cakes.

thought: his great ancestor's shadow
line: Franizzard Van Lumbcook. Big boots to fill, and I've small feet.

thought: still doesn't know when the Duke's birthday is
line: It was never the Duke's birthday. I still don't know when it is.

thought: a job for life by inheritance; he'd like to earn it
line: A job for life, from an ancestor. I'd like to earn it myself, one day.

thought: checks every recipe now for anything magical
line: I read every recipe twice now, for anything... magical. Just in case.

thought: the guests frozen at a feast he cooked
line: Oh, the guests! Frozen stiff at the table, and over my cooking.

thought: plain cooking from now on
line: Plain cakes from now on. Burnt, I expect, but plain.

thought: the Duke is still speaking to him, somehow
line: Weeellll... the Duke's still speaking to me. That's something.

thought: the player saved the feast and his job
line: The whole feast saved, my friend, and the cook along with it!

thought: without the player that recipe would have finished them
line: Without you, that recipe would have been the end of us all.

thought: even his ancestor never had such help
line: Even my great ancestor never had help like you, my friend.

thought: tested them with a fake birthday; they passed
line: I tested you with a birthday that wasn't. You passed, and then some.

thought: the Culinaromancer is done for, and so nearly were they
line: Ooh, it's you! The Culinaromancer's done for, and so nearly were we.

thought: if he ever becomes a great cook, half the credit is theirs
line: If I'm ever a great cook, my friend, it'll be half your doing.

thought: every guest came out alive
line: Every guest came out of it alive, thanks to you. Every one!

thought: the big cheeses owe the player their lives
line: My friend, the big cheeses owe you their lives. Not that they'll say.

thought: sulks: anyone could have used the wrong recipe
line: Don't look at me like that. Anyone could have used the wrong recipe.

thought: a feast in the player's honour would only burn
line: A feast in your honour? I'd burn it, and then where would we be?

thought: the player saved everyone; he did all the cooking
line: Yes, yes, you saved everyone. Some of us did all the cooking.

thought: suspects the hero wants a seat at the Duke's table
line: Oh, the hero of the feast. Wanting a seat at the Duke's table now?

thought: the player never asked whose birthday it really was
line: You never asked if it was really the Duke's birthday. Trusting sort.

thought: would thank properly but the player would want feeding
line: I'd thank you properly, but you'd only want feeding.

thought: keep away from the old cookbook
line: Mind you don't touch that old cookbook. Look what happened last time.

thought: beat the Culinaromancer, but can they bake
line: You beat the Culinaromancer. Could you make a cake that doesn't burn?

thought: opened the shutters and only light came in
line: Opened the shutters this morning. Nothing came in but the light.

thought: what to do with all that garlic
line: What do I do with all this garlic now? Cook with it, I suppose.

thought: still sleeps with a scarf on, from habit
line: Still sleep with the scarf on. Old habits, that's all it is.

thought: the village is still named after him
line: Still named after him, this village. Somebody ought to see to that.

thought: rereads the legends to be sure it's over
line: Staked, and gone. I've read the legends twice over to be sure.

thought: walked towards the manor, nearly
line: Walked past the manor gate today. Well, near it. Well, towards it.

thought: he always said the Count had to be stopped
line: I always said he had to be stopped. And now he has been.

thought: many failed; then came his hero
line: The legends are full of folk who failed. Not my hero, though.

thought: sees the hero again and thanks them again
line: Oh! It's you again! Have I thanked you today? Thank you!

thought: points out the one who staked the Count
line: Draynor owes that one so much. Staked the Count, they did!

thought: sleeps through the night now
line: I sleep the whole night through now, adventurer. All thanks to you.

thought: knew it on first sight, or hoped it
line: Bold adventurer! I knew it the moment I saw you. Well, I hoped it.

thought: did what the ones in the legends couldn't
line: You did what all the others in the legends never could.

thought: tells everyone about the player; they've stopped listening
line: I tell everyone about you. They've stopped listening, but I tell them.

thought: offers all his garlic
line: If ever you need garlic, adventurer, mine's yours. All of it.

thought: his neck is the most grateful part of him
line: My neck thanks you most of all, brave adventurer. Bless you.

thought: staked a vampyre and still no garlic
line: You staked a vampyre and still go about without garlic? Honestly.

thought: took so long he nearly ran out of garlic
line: Took your time with the Count. I nearly ran out of garlic.

thought: he did all the reading
line: Don't let it go to your head. I did all the reading.

thought: walked into that manor without a care
line: You walked right into that manor without a care. Reckless, I call it.

thought: manor dust on the boots
line: Hero or not, you'll knock the manor dust off before you come in.

thought: never thanked for the warning
line: You never once thanked me for the warning, you know.

thought: some of them were frightened the whole time
line: Don't look so pleased. Some of us were frightened the whole time.

thought: the hero gets the credit, the worrier gets nothing
line: You get called a hero. I get called jumpy. Hardly fair, is it?

thought: thinks of adding wigs to the business, royal custom and all
line: Ned's Handmade Wigs, I could call it. Royal custom, an' all.

thought: same hands make rope and wigs
line: Wigs and rope, both from wool. Same hands, different knots.

thought: his wool sat on royalty; probably itched
line: Never thought old Ned's wool would sit on royalty. Itchy, I'd expect.

thought: a prince escaped in his wig and no rum came of it
line: Prince got clean away in my wig, and not a drop of rum came of it.

thought: proud of the tight work that fooled a kidnapper
line: Lady Keli never looked twice at that wig. Good tight work, that.

thought: if a wig fools a kidnapper, think of his rope
line: If a wool wig can fool a kidnapper, think what my rope could do.

thought: can't wait to brag at the docks
line: A prince in one of me wigs. Wait till I tells 'em down the docks.

thought: wool is wool, whatever it ends up as
line: Wool's wool. Rope one day, a prince's hair the next.

thought: points out the one who smuggled a prince in his wig
line: There goes the one who smuggled a prince out in old Ned's wig.

thought: the player knew where to come for a wig
line: You knew where to come for a wig. Clever, that. Old Ned's the best.

thought: got the prince home under his wool; proud of them both
line: Got that prince home under my wool, didn't you? Proud of us both.

thought: Ned's wool and the player's nerve
line: A prince saved by Ned's wool and your nerve. I likes that.

thought: not many would think of a wig
line: Proper rescuer, you are. Not many'd have thought of a wig.

thought: anything in wool for the player, bar jumpers
line: Anything you want in wool, old Ned's yours. Bar jumpers.

thought: the player has a sailor's nerve
line: You've the nerve for a rescue. Sailor's nerve, I calls it.

thought: the prince's kidnappers were nothing to the monsters he's fought, but well done
line: Kidnappers ain't monsters, but you saw 'em off all the same. Good.

thought: asked for a wig; next it'll be a bonnet
line: Asked old Ned for a wig, did you? Next you'll want a bonnet.

thought: made a wig, but they still won't buy his rope
line: Wigs for princes, aye. But you'll still not buy my rope.

thought: folk will think he's gone soft
line: Folk'll think old Ned's gone soft, making wigs for the likes of you.

thought: sailed the seas and ended up doing hair
line: A wig! I sailed the seas, and you had me doing hair.

thought: no matching beard; he has his pride
line: Don't go asking for a matching beard. Old Ned has his pride.

thought: no tot of rum for the wig
line: Saved a prince with my wool, and never a tot of rum for old Ned.

thought: the player would make a poor prince
line: You'd make a poor prince, you would. Wig'd slip off at the gate.

thought: laughing at his wigs is a mistake monsters have made
line: Laughing at old Ned's wigs? Monsters have tried that, and lost.

thought: the prince is home and he can go back to being ignored
line: Prince Ali is home, and the city has gone back to ignoring me. Good.

thought: sq'irk juice is purely professional
line: Sq'irk juice sharpens the fingers. I take it purely for the work.

thought: the sorceress gives him no more fruit
line: She gives me no more fruit. We had words, once. That is all.

thought: his daughter says nothing of her work, as taught
line: My daughter says nothing of her work. I taught her well.

thought: a rescue without bodies is how it should be done
line: A rescue with no bodies. That is how such things should be done.

thought: keeps a short list for dangerous work
line: I keep a short list for dangerous work. It is shorter than one thinks.

thought: juice before noon, for the fingers
line: Juice before noon? A spymaster must keep his fingers light.

thought: the Menaphites will have heard; let them wonder
line: The Menaphites will have heard of the rescue. Let them wonder how.

thought: formal greeting to someone tested
line: Hello again. You did that job quietly. I have not forgotten.

thought: the player never boasted of the rescue
line: You have not boasted of the rescue in the market. I noticed.

thought: professional work; rare praise
line: Professional work, that rescue. I do not say so often.

thought: Leela has promoted the player
line: Leela has stopped calling you 'the stranger'. That is a promotion.

thought: the player is filed under useful now
line: You are filed under 'useful' now. Few are. Fewer stay there.

thought: not a word about the prince from the player
line: Not one word from you about the prince, all this time. Good.

thought: the player walks past the palace as if they belong; earned
line: You walk past the palace as though you belong. You have earned it.

thought: trusts nobody, distrusts this one a little less
line: I do not trust people. You I distrust a little less.

thought: the prince is rescued; stop looking pleased
line: You again. The prince is rescued; you may stop looking pleased.

thought: a spy is never famous; the player now is
line: A spy is never famous. You, I fear, have become famous.

thought: won't share his sq'irk juice
line: Do not ask me for sq'irk juice. I have barely enough for myself.

thought: hoping to be a spy now? still no
line: If you are hoping to be a spy now, the answer is still no.

thought: the job is done, no song
line: You did the job. Do not make a song of it.

thought: strolling past the palace again
line: Strolling past the palace again. Old habits, or are you lost?

thought: Hassan calls the player a friend; of course he would
line: Hassan calls you a friend of the city. Hassan would.

thought: lucky once; not twice
line: Lucky, that rescue. I would not count on luck twice.

thought: Irena no longer watches the gate
line: Irena has stopped watching the gate. I almost miss her company.

thought: Ana home and already eyeing the dunes
line: Ana is home, and already eyeing the dunes again. That girl!

thought: next time Ana passes she reads the billboard
line: Next time Ana passes, she reads the billboard first. Twice.

thought: the waterskin he kept for the girl can be sold now
line: The waterskin I kept for the girl... I suppose I can sell it now.

thought: quiet gate, happy mother
line: A quiet gate and a happy mother. A warden asks for nothing more.

thought: the desert rarely gives anyone back
line: The desert gave one back. It does not do that often.

thought: Irena smiles at everyone, even the toll
line: Irena smiles at everyone now. Even at the toll.

thought: the toll covers repairs and wages, nothing more
line: Repairs to the gate, wages for my men, and not a coin over.

thought: knows who to thank for Ana
line: Hello again, friend. Irena's girl is home, and I know who to thank.

thought: points out who brought Ana home
line: There goes the one who brought Ana home. My gate salutes them.

thought: walked into the sands and out with a child
line: You walked into the sands and walked out with a child. Remarkable.

thought: a mother sleeps because of the player
line: A mother sleeps at night because of you, friend. No small thing.

thought: sells waterskins to many, tips his hat to few
line: I sell waterskins to many. I tip my hat to very few, friend.

thought: the sands gave the player back, and the girl too
line: The sands gave you back, friend, and brought the girl along too.

thought: still has to see the pass, a little
line: No need for a pass, friend. Well, a little need. Rules are rules.

thought: a rescuer who still pays the toll
line: A rescuer who still pays the toll. You are a credit, friend.

thought: Ana's home; stop looking pleased at his gate
line: Ana is home, friend. You may stop looking so pleased at my gate.

thought: did they read the billboard first? no
line: Brought the girl back, yes. Did you read the billboard first? No.

thought: if Ana runs off again, the player can fetch her
line: If Ana runs off again, you can fetch her. I have a gate to mind.

thought: hero of the desert, still haggles over the toll
line: Hero of the desert, and still you haggle over a small toll.

thought: saving girls is good; so is buying a robe
line: Saving girls in the desert is good work. So is paying for a robe.

thought: the cell's still there; heroes need it too
line: The cell is still there, friend. Heroes have been known to need it.

thought: a hero will want a free drink now
line: A hero at my gate. I suppose you will want a cool drink for nothing.

thought: found one lost girl; now find the end of the queue
line: You found one lost girl, friend. Now find the end of my queue.

thought: fooling a troll Mother at his age, from a coffin
line: Oh dear, oh dear. Fooling a troll Mother at my age, and from a coffin.

thought: if he must lie in a coffin, it'll be good wood
line: Mahogany, that coffin. If I'm to lie in one, it'll be good wood.

thought: drove Mother's band out in his youth; she remembers
line: Drove Mother's band out of those tunnels in my youth. She remembers.

thought: playing dead is harder than it looks
line: Playing dead is harder than it looks. Especially after a big lunch.

thought: has slept in worse places than a coffin
line: I've slept in worse places than a coffin. Entrana's beds, for one.

thought: money doesn't matter once you have plenty
line: Money doesn't matter once you've as much as I have. Remember that.

thought: denies snoring; it was the wood creaking
line: I don't snore. That was the coffin, creaking. Mahogany creaks.

thought: lay so still he nearly fooled himself
line: Lay so still in that box, I nearly fooled myself.

thought: the player would have done well against Mother's lot
line: You'd have done well against Mother's lot. Nearly as well as me.

thought: trusts the player not to tell about the snoring
line: Ah, the young hero! You'd never tell about the snoring, would you?

thought: good to see the player up and about, unlike some
line: Good to see you up and about, my dear. Some of us had to lie in boxes.

thought: the player has the nerve for trolls, as he did once
line: You've the nerve for trolls, I'll give you that. I had it once, too.

thought: the one he'd trust with his coffin
line: Of all the young heroes, you're the one I'd trust with my coffin.

thought: a credit to the new generation, almost to the old
line: A credit to the new generation, you are. Almost a credit to the old.

thought: never laughed about the coffin, to his face
line: You never laughed at me about the coffin. Well, not to my face.

thought: would make a fine sage; learn to snore quietly
line: You'd make a fine sage one day. Learn to snore quietly first.

thought: don't tell the village about the snoring
line: Don't you dare tell the village about the snoring. Not a word.

thought: he was playing dead; the player manages it without trying
line: I was only playing dead. You, I hear, manage it without trying.

thought: stop grinning; anyone would snore in mahogany
line: Less of the grinning, young lad. You'd snore too, in mahogany.

thought: trolls at his age, and the player stood about
line: Trolls, at my age! And you just stood about, I expect.

thought: drove trolls from tunnels; the player would struggle with a cellar
line: I've driven trolls out of tunnels. You'd struggle with a cellar.

thought: a coffin is no excuse to inherit the hat
line: Staring at my hat again? A coffin doesn't mean you inherit it.

thought: the player can't tell a dead sage from a sleeping one; Mother could
line: Can't tell a dead sage from a sleeping one? Mother could, worse luck.

thought: thinks themselves brave; he lay in a box beside a troll
line: Think yourself brave? I lay in a box beside a troll, young lad.

thought: heard Romeo still bolts from Juliet
line: Word is Romeo still runs off shrieking about ghosts. Sad, really.

thought: his potion did its job too well for Romeo
line: My potion worked a treat. Too well, by Romeo's account.

thought: he never thought much of the lad
line: Always thought that Romeo lad was a bit strange. Still do.

thought: no more call for odd orders, back to the usual
line: No call for cadava potions now. Strength potions again, then.

thought: leftover ingredients on the shelf
line: Wing of rat, ear of snake... I've half a jar of each going spare.

thought: heard the lad's moved on to the cousin
line: Romeo's sweet on the cousin now, I hear. Phillipa, isn't it?

thought: sad affair, but the brewing was sound
line: Sad business, that. Still, the potion did just what it said.

thought: nobody wants to hear the recipe twice
line: Nobody asks what goes in a cadava potion twice.

thought: the player never blabbed about the potion
line: You kept quiet about that potion. I do value a quiet customer.

thought: the plan was good, Romeo spoiled it
line: Not your fault the lad's a fool. The plan was sound.

thought: business offer to a trusted customer
line: Need to look dead for a while, friend? I'll mix it. For a price.

thought: his courier, and the potion got there whole
line: Huzzah, my courier! The potion got there in one piece, I hear.

thought: would hire them if he weren't so tight
line: You'd make a fair apothecary's runner. Pity I can't afford one.

thought: tells someone this one did the job properly
line: That one helped with my potion. Did it properly, too.

thought: dry relief that the death was only for show
line: Ah, friend. All that fuss, and nobody actually died.

thought: they look healthier than Romeo does these days
line: You look well. Better than Romeo, who still shrieks at Juliet.

thought: the player meddled and Romeo sees ghosts now
line: You meddled, and now Romeo shrieks at the sight of Juliet.

thought: teasing they want a second go
line: Back for another dead-looking potion? One per customer, I think.

thought: the matchmaking went to the wrong girl
line: Some matchmaker. The lad left with the cousin.

thought: suspects they want a discount for helping
line: Helped a girl look dead, and now you want a discount? Hardly.

thought: warns a neighbour about the player
line: Mind that one. Last time, somebody ended up in a crypt.

thought: business advice: get paid first
line: Next time a lad wants help with his love life, ask for coin first.

thought: keeps them away from the berries
line: Hands off the cadava berries. One sad love story's plenty.

thought: they kept the secret, which is useless to a gossip
line: Discreet, aren't you? Too discreet to be any use for gossip.

thought: no demon left to watch, and the ball is idle
line: No demon in the mists now. The ball hardly knows what to show me.

thought: she judges the deed against her old hero
line: A good bit of demon-slaying, that. Wally would have approved.

thought: heard the museum changed its card
line: They've a new card by the museum's sword now, I hear. Quite right.

thought: she foresaw the hero but not how young
line: The demon I saw coming. A hero quite so young, I did not.

thought: back to ordinary fortunes
line: Back to weddings and weather in the ball. Peaceful, I suppose.

thought: Wally is still forgotten, which still rankles
line: Wally still gets no song, mind. Some things the ball can't mend.

thought: the circle feels different now the demon is down
line: The stone circle feels cold now. Cold is much better than red.

thought: her blessing seems to have worked
line: Guthix was with the young one after all. I did ask him nicely.

thought: greets the hero, the city is quieter
line: There's my hero. The ball shows a quieter city, thanks to you.

thought: pleased to be proved right by someone else's work
line: It's nice to be right, young one, and nicer when you do the work.

thought: Silverlight in good hands again
line: Wally's sword found a worthy hand again. He'd have liked you, dear.

thought: a fond near-offer of a free reading
line: I'd read your fortune for nothing today, dear. Well, nearly nothing.

thought: points out how young the demon-slayer is
line: Look at that one. Young as anything, and a demon behind them.

thought: the young turned out useful after all
line: The young are good for something after all! Ye gods, who knew?

thought: history forgot Wally, she won't let it forget this one
line: History forgot Wally. I'll see to it that it doesn't forget you.

thought: the ball was right about them
line: So the ball was right about you. It usually is, but I do enjoy it.

thought: one demon and they swagger like Wally
line: One demon, and already you walk like Wally. He walked better.

thought: a demon-slayer still can't guess her next word
line: Beat a demon, and still you can't guess what I'll say next.

thought: don't let it go to their head
line: Don't let one demon go to your head, dear. There's not much room.

thought: the ball saw them win, not how slowly
line: The ball showed you winning. It didn't show you taking so long.

thought: a demon-slayer who still won't heed her warnings
line: That one sealed a demon. Still won't heed me about the Wilderness.

thought: still a babe to someone her age
line: Saved the city, and you're still a babe in arms to me, young one.

thought: asks them to hurry next time
line: Next demon, do be quicker. I'm not getting any younger, you know.

thought: they'd spoil any future she gave them
line: I'd tell you your future, young one, but you'd only go and spoil it.

thought: still delighted the mine can be reached
line: The essence mine, reachable again! I still can't quite believe it.

thought: his shop now buys as well as sells
line: Buying runes back now, as well as selling. A proper rune man's shop.

thought: so many want sending to the mine he's hoarse
line: Everyone wants teleporting to the mine now. My voice is going.

thought: words lost in the fire, now said every day
line: The old tower lost those words when it burned. Now I say them daily.

thought: the notes matter more now they work
line: Must lock away the coded notes. Both sets. Now especially.

thought: runecraft is alive again in his shop
line: Essence in, runes out. Runecraft is a living art again.

thought: Reldo will want to write it up
line: Reldo will want a book written about all this. I'll want it first.

thought: his day now runs on tea and teleports
line: Tea, then the mine, then more tea. That's the order of things now.

thought: remembers who opened the mine
line: The mine's open because of you, adventurer. I've not forgotten.

thought: offers the helper a trip
line: Fancy a trip to the mine, adventurer? It's the least I can do.

thought: keen to buy runes from this particular helper
line: Any runes you make, I'll buy. From you especially.

thought: points out who brought the secret back
line: There goes the one who carried the old tower's secret back to us.

thought: they gave an old art back to him
line: You've given an old art back to us, adventurer. Well, to me, mostly.

thought: the good tea for them
line: For you, adventurer, the good tea. The rest get the dusty sort.

thought: greets his courier, still selling
line: Ah, my favourite courier! Mind you, I'd still sell you a rune.

thought: Sedridor surely thinks well of them
line: Sedridor speaks well of you, I'd wager. He certainly ought to.

thought: free trips, no purchases
line: Off to the mine on my say-so, and still not one rune bought. Honestly.

thought: no runes brought back to sell
line: All that essence you've mined, and I've yet to see a rune from it.

thought: threatens to charge for the trips
line: Back for another free trip? I'll start charging tea money.

thought: teases the slow delivery of the notes
line: You did carry those notes the long way round, didn't you?

thought: doubts they could say the incantation
line: The incantation isn't long, but you'd still muddle it, I expect.

thought: they fetched for both wizards
line: Fetched for Sedridor, fetched for me. Do you ever fetch for yourself?

thought: essence dust tracked in
line: Mind the essence dust, adventurer. You trail it in every time.

thought: helped revive runecraft but can't tell runes apart
line: Revived a lost art, and still muddles mind runes with body runes.

thought: casts made, the order is safe
line: Casts made, clay to spare. Nurmof will have his order on time.

thought: both anvils busy again
line: Both anvils ringing again. That's the sound of a happy smithy.

thought: well stocked for once
line: Plenty of clay in the store now. I'll not be short for a while.

thought: his promise to his helper stands
line: My friend's welcome at these anvils any time. I meant that.

thought: wonders how the helper's smithing goes
line: Wonder how my friend's metalworking is coming along. Must ask.

thought: Nurmof has nothing to grumble about now
line: Iron in, pickaxes out. Nurmof's had no cause to grumble lately.

thought: feels he underpaid for the ore
line: A few coins for all that ore. Ought to have been more, really.

thought: someone's used the anvils, as they should
line: Someone's been at my anvils again. Good. That's what they're for.

thought: greets the friend who brought the ore
line: Hello again, friend! My anvils are always free for you.

thought: asks after their smithing
line: How's your metalworking coming along, friend? Well, I hope.

thought: points out the one who fetched his clay
line: There's the friend who fetched my clay. A good day's work, that was.

thought: their copper made good pickaxes
line: The pickaxes from your copper are some of my best, friend.

thought: they have the makings of a smith
line: You've the makings of a smith, friend. My anvils say so.

thought: the order went out thanks to them
line: Nurmof's order went out on time, friend, and that's thanks to you.

thought: the ore was honest and clean
line: Good honest ore you brought me. Not a speck of rubbish in it.

thought: always time for a friend
line: Anvils hot or not, there's always time for a friend out here.

thought: welcome at the anvils, but careful
line: Use my anvils by all means, friend. Do try not to dent them.

thought: they hoped for a bigger reward
line: A few coins for all that ore, and you look as if you'd hoped for more.

thought: the iron took a while, forgiven
line: Took your time with that iron, friend. I'll not hold it against you.

thought: free anvils, unused
line: Free use of my anvils, and still you smith elsewhere? How kind.

thought: deflates the hero: clay-fetching is small work
line: My clay-fetcher! Not much call for heroes out here, I'm afraid.

thought: a fallback trade if adventuring fails
line: There's always work fetching clay, friend, if adventuring dries up.

thought: anvils are for smithing
line: Mind, friend, the anvils are for smithing. Not for sitting on.

thought: welcome everywhere but the wheat
line: That one's welcome at my anvils and my door. Just not in my wheat.

thought: Fluffs is back where she belongs
line: Fluffs back on my knee, purring away. All's right with the world.

thought: the house is full of kittens now
line: Kittens in every basket! Who'd have thought one cat could do all this?

thought: it was only the kitten she was fretting for
line: All that fuss, and she only wanted her kitten. Cats, honestly.

thought: still amazed where Fluffs was found
line: The Lumber Yard, of all places! Fluffs never did like a tidy spot.

thought: kittens to spare, but only to good homes
line: Kittens to spare, if anyone wants one. Fed and stroked, mind.

thought: has a medal waiting for a good ratter
line: Medal's ready for the next young cat that does its bit with the rats.

thought: two cats to feed now
line: Sardines for Fluffs, sardines for the kitten. I'll need a bigger pan.

thought: Fluffs acts as if Gertrude was the one lost
line: Fluffs looks at me as if I'm the one who went missing. Cats!

thought: greets the one who brought Fluffs home
line: Oh, it's you, dear! Fluffs purrs whenever you go by, you know.

thought: tells a neighbour who found Fluffs
line: That's the one who found my Fluffs, that is. Saved my wits.

thought: a medal for a good ratter
line: If you've a young cat, dear, there's a medal in it for a good ratter.

thought: she sleeps again with Fluffs home
line: Bless you, dear. I sleep at night again, with Fluffs on my feet.

thought: they searched the Lumber Yard for a cat
line: Into the Lumber Yard for my cat! Not many would, dear.

thought: both cats home thanks to the player
line: Fluffs and her kitten both home, and all thanks to you, dear.

thought: any kitten would be lucky with them
line: Any kitten of mine would be lucky to go home with you, dear.

thought: they do their bit, like a good cat
line: You do your bit, dear. I like that in a person. And in a cat.

thought: kittens underfoot, and it's their fault
line: Mind where you tread, dear. Kittens everywhere now, thanks to you.

thought: it took them a while
line: Took you long enough to find her, dear. Still, she's home.

thought: backhanded: Fluffs has grown less fussy
line: Fluffs likes you now, dear. She's less fussy than she used to be.

thought: good at finding cats, now fix the boys
line: You're very good at finding cats, dear. Now find my boys a hobby.

thought: the obvious place, surely
line: The Lumber Yard! You'd think an adventurer would look there first.

thought: medals are for cats, not people
line: Medals are for cats who catch rats, dear. None for people, I'm afraid.

thought: warns it mustn't go to their head
line: That one found my cat. Don't let it go to their head, mind.

thought: no more rewards, only kittens
line: After another reward, dear? I've only kittens, and plenty of those.

thought: the new room is big enough to get lost in
line: A palaeontology room downstairs! My word, I still get lost in it.

thought: the fossils keep coming, each better
line: Fossils from the island, and every one more incredible than the last.

thought: bones below, cake baking
line: Bones in the basement, cake in the oven. A fine day at the museum.

thought: the labels for the new room aren't done
line: Must finish the labels downstairs. One can't have unlabelled bones.

thought: delighted he can name the island at last
line: Fossil Island! I may say it out loud now. Fossil Island!

thought: great lengths, this time over water
line: Great lengths for a treasure, I say. This time, across the water.

thought: children climbing the new bones
line: Children adore the new bones. I do wish they'd stop climbing them.

thought: heard what was in the sailors' potion
line: Mostly vodka, those sealegs potions, I hear. Sailors swear by them.

thought: greets the explorer behind the new room
line: Ah, our island explorer! The new room downstairs is half your doing.

thought: urges them to see the fossils they made possible
line: Have you seen the new fossils downstairs? You must. You found the way.

thought: cake for the one who opened the island
line: There's cake for whoever opened up Fossil Island. That's you, I think.

thought: hopes they've brought more bones
line: My word, the voyager returns! Any more bones for us? No? Pity.

thought: points the explorer out to a visitor
line: That one sailed off and came back with history. Incredible!

thought: the fossils would thank them if they could
line: If the fossils could talk, they'd thank you. I'll have to do instead.

thought: glad they came back safe from the island
line: Splendid to see you back on dry land, and all in one piece!

thought: they have the museum's spirit
line: You've the museum's spirit, you know. Off to an island for old bones!

thought: keep their elbows off the fossils
line: Mind the fossils, please. They've lasted ages without your elbows.

thought: opened an island, still no eye for fossils
line: Opened up an island, and still you can't tell a fossil from a pebble?

thought: suspects they'd trade a fossil away
line: You'd swap a fossil for a pint, I expect. Not in my museum.

thought: deflates the explorer: the bones did the work
line: You found the island, and the bones did the rest. Let's be honest.

thought: they came back smelling of the sea
line: That one went to sea for science. Came back smelling of it, too.

thought: cake is for exams, not voyages
line: Cake is for passing exams. Sailing doesn't count, I'm afraid.

thought: no climbing the skeletons
line: Don't climb the skeletons. The children do quite enough of that.

thought: the explorer reads labels like everyone else
line: Our island explorer, back to read the labels like everyone else.

thought: the temple soldiers can wait
line: Soldiers for Paterdomus, yes, yes. Once other priorities are balanced.

thought: the river is blessed again, at the cost of a dog
line: The Salve blessed afresh, and Drezel freed. And only the one dog lost.

thought: it cost the crown nothing
line: Drezel free, the river blessed, and not a coin spent. Splendid.

thought: promises his advisor he'll see to the Zamorakians
line: Zamorakians in Saradomin's temple. I shall get round to it, Aeonisig.

thought: still baffled by the dog
line: A guard dog, of all things. I still cannot fathom it.

thought: the Salve keeps the kingdom safe again
line: The vampyres stay over the Salve, where Saradomin intends them.

thought: the treasury against the temple
line: The temple wants soldiers, and the treasury wants a rest. Hmm.

thought: pretends he never worried about Drezel
line: Old Drezel set free. I always said the fellow would turn up.

thought: thanks that talk down
line: Ah, Drezel's rescuer. Your king is pleased, which ought to be plenty.

thought: grants them a little credit
line: The Salve runs blessed again, citizen. You may take a little credit.

thought: tells his advisor to look pious
line: Aeonisig, the temple's rescuer is passing. Look pious, man.

thought: praise with one exception
line: You did well at Paterdomus, adventurer. Apart from the dog.

thought: the kingdom is safer, modestly
line: Saradomin's kingdom is the safer for you, citizen. Modestly so.

thought: graciously allows approach
line: Good heavens, it is the temple's rescuer. You may approach. Slowly.

thought: has nearly forgiven the dog
line: I have forgiven you the dog, citizen. Very nearly. A royal kindness.

thought: a medal he would only consider
line: Had I a medal for rescuing priests, citizen, I would consider it.

thought: the dog-slayer, mocked
line: Ah, the dog-slayer. Did you see off any kittens on the way home?

thought: sent to help, not to cull
line: A temple dog, citizen. You were sent to help, not to thin the kennels.

thought: rescuing a priest by killing his dog
line: Only you would rescue a priest by slaying his dog first, citizen.

thought: soldiers will come in due course
line: Soldiers for the temple? In due course, citizen. Do stop asking.

thought: no reward after the dog
line: A reward? You killed the temple's dog. Let us call it even, citizen.

thought: protect the palace bear from the dog-killer
line: The palace bear stays in its cage today, Aeonisig. Look who is here.

thought: next time he'll send someone fonder of dogs
line: Next time a priest wants looking in on, I shall send a dog lover.

thought: dismisses them: the Salve is seen to, and so is the dog
line: Run along, citizen. The Salve is seen to, and so, alas, is the dog.

thought: his dragonfire theory has a hole in it
line: Shield soaks up the fire, and it goes... where? That's what I'd know.

thought: someone actually slew the Crandor dragon
line: Somebody slew the dragon of Crandor. Didn't think I'd see the day.

thought: the plate is finally for sale, to a dragon slayer
line: My plate's finally for sale. Only took a dragon.

thought: the maze keys aren't his trouble now
line: Melzar's keys? Guildmaster's business now. Not mine.

thought: the visage legend, rare as anything
line: A visage, now. Dragonkin made, they say. Rarer than a quiet day.

thought: he owned up he was wrong, once
line: Owned up I was wrong. Don't make a habit of it, mind.

thought: the dragonfire shield is steep work at a steep price
line: Dragonfire shield's a steep job. Master smith's price, too.

thought: now he has a real hero to compare the peacocks to
line: Guildmaster still sends his peacocks. Now I've a real hero to compare.

thought: gruff greeting for the dragon slayer
line: Aye, there's my dragon-slaying friend. Forge is always warm for ye.

thought: won't doubt them again
line: Doubted ye once. Won't make that mistake twice.

thought: the plate is theirs to buy
line: Plate's yours to buy whenever ye like. Ye've earned it.

thought: best the Guildmaster ever sent, grudgingly
line: Best the Guildmaster ever sent me. Don't tell him I said so.

thought: offers his finest work, at his price
line: Bring me a visage and I'll make ye a shield worth having. At a price.

thought: real deeds, unlike the others
line: Real deeds, that one. Not like the fancy-pants lot.

thought: lets the hero linger, briefly
line: A dragon slayer at my door. Sit, if ye must. Briefly.

thought: curious whether the shield held
line: Ye'll have smelt dragonfire close up. Shield hold, did it?

thought: a dragon doesn't buy a discount
line: One dragon slain, and still ye can't haggle a master smith down.

thought: still walks in without knocking
line: Dragon slayer or no, ye still walk in without knocking.

thought: the keys are someone else's job
line: Still on about the maze keys? I'm a smith, not a key cupboard.

thought: one apology is all they get
line: Apologised once. Ye'll not get another out of me, adventurer.

thought: they took their time with the dragon
line: Slew a dragon, aye. Took ye long enough, mind.

thought: questions instead of visages
line: Mighty dragon slayer, and ye still bring me questions, not visages.

thought: the swagger has come back
line: There goes the hero. Swagger's grown back already, I see.

thought: they couldn't afford the shield fee
line: Dragonfire shield? Ye couldn't afford the fee, slayer or no.

thought: annotates the history with the news
line: I've pencilled a note in Wright's history: shield found, in halves.

thought: the book never guessed where the halves were
line: Half with each gang, all those years. Wright never guessed that.

thought: for once the histories were right
line: Arrav's shield back in the museum. The histories were right, for once.

thought: his advice to check at the museum paid off
line: I sent the finder to the museum to have it checked. Genuine, too.

thought: must keep up with gang history
line: Must read up on the Black Arm again. One hates to be out of date.

thought: hopes his old pupil read the certificate himself
line: The king paid up, I hear. I do hope he read the certificate himself.

thought: Arrav would approve, if the tales hold
line: Arrav would have been pleased, I think. Assuming the tales are right.

thought: lost the very book again
line: Now, where did I put Wright's history? I only just had it out.

thought: their deed made a history book current
line: Ah, my favourite reader! You turned a history book into news.

thought: they read before they acted
line: You read the book first. Most adventurers skip straight to the gangs.

thought: proud one of his readers did it
line: Half a shield, brought home by one of my readers. I'm rather proud.

thought: history was done a kindness
line: You did history a kindness, friend. It so rarely gets one.

thought: recounts it aloud with satisfaction
line: Let's see... shield found, reward paid. And by you! Ah, yes.

thought: a deed done by a reader
line: A real deed, done by someone who reads! I'd hoped I'd live to see it.

thought: curious, for the record, how they got in
line: I'd love to know how you got in with that gang. For the record.

thought: Arrav would tip his hat, if the tales are true
line: Arrav himself would tip his hat to you, if the tales are true.

thought: only half the shield
line: Half a shield! Was the other half too heavy for you, I wonder?

thought: a former gang member among his books
line: A gang member, in my library? I'll be counting the books tonight.

thought: they creased his book
line: You returned Wright's history with a crease in it. I did notice.

thought: either gang would have them
line: Phoenix or Black Arm, which was it? You'd pass for either, frankly.

thought: one shield, and still no other reading
line: One shield found, and you've still not read anything else, have you?

thought: joined a gang when a book would do
line: Joined a gang for the sake of history. I'd have simply read about it.

thought: the tale grows each time they tell it
line: Do stop telling it bigger each time. That's how folk tales start.

thought: a gang member looking innocent
line: That one ran with a gang, and now looks innocent in a library. Hmm.

thought: still mourning, after a fashion
line: Poor dear Juliet. Terrible business. I've worn my sad face all week.

thought: saw the ghost on the balcony again and ran
line: Saw Juliet's ghost again! Up on the balcony! I ran ever so fast.

thought: can't keep hold of the new name either
line: Phillipa. Philippa? Pillipa. Lovely name, whichever it is.

thought: the flowers have a new recipient
line: Flowers for Phillipa now. Juliet would understand, being a ghost.

thought: confuses the ghost with the old balcony throwing
line: Do ghosts throw things? Because Juliet's ghost throws things.

thought: can't recall where it all happened
line: Ermmm... was it a crypt or a cellar? Somewhere damp and sad, anyway.

thought: his hero ambitions undone by one ghost
line: I'd be a hero if I weren't frightened of ghosts. Well, one ghost.

thought: swears to remember Juliet, and can't
line: Juliet... Julia... the poor one. I'll always remember her. Mostly.

thought: admires their nerve in the crypt business
line: You were so brave about all that crypt business, my friend!

thought: muddled thanks for meeting Phillipa
line: Without you I'd never have met Phillipa, so golly, thank you!

thought: they carried his messages faithfully
line: You carried all my messages and never once read them. Or did you?

thought: shares his flowers
line: Have a flower, my friend! I've plenty. Phillipa gets the rest.

thought: tells someone this is the hero of his tragedy
line: That one's a real hero, that is. Saw me through my tragedy!

thought: relieved they're not a ghost
line: Golly, you look like someone who isn't a ghost. That's lovely.

thought: grateful they were there at the sad bit
line: Thank you for being there when Juliet... ermmm... you know.

thought: they rank second only to Phillipa
line: Wooooo! My favourite friend! Second favourite. Phillipa's first.

thought: tactless about pallor and ghosts
line: Are you a ghost? You're very pale. Juliet was pale, and look at her.

thought: accidentally reminds them they were meant to save her
line: You were meant to save Juliet, weren't you? Ermmm... never mind.

thought: they'd frighten a ghost, kindly meant
line: You look like someone who'd frighten a ghost, in a nice way!

thought: worried they'd blab to Phillipa
line: Don't tell Phillipa you knew Juliet. You've a blabbing sort of face.

thought: misremembers who his messenger was
line: You carried my messages? I thought it was the taller one.

thought: startled by them, then tactless
line: There's a ghost behind you! Oh, no, it's only your face.

thought: blames them for the potion, cheerfully
line: Golly, was it you who brought her that potion? Bit careless, friend.

thought: they look gloomier than he does
line: You've a sad, crypty sort of look. Cheer up, like I did!

thought: still amazed at the cabbage
line: A cabbage. Years of witchcraft undone by a cabbage. I still marvel.

thought: the demands were withdrawn
line: The Black Knights withdrew every demand. Saradomin be thanked.

thought: cabbages look different to him now
line: I find I cannot look at a cabbage in the same way now.

thought: the fee left the purse lighter
line: That fee for the fortress business has left the order lighter still.

thought: back to the long quiet
line: Back to proper quiet, and no real crisis in years. Long may it last.

thought: years of brewing spoilt by a vegetable
line: Years their witch spent on that potion. Years! Spoilt by a vegetable.

thought: the Black Knights are sulking
line: Let them sulk in their fortress. They have earned a good sulk.

thought: tells the corgi off the cabbages
line: Sir Burrus is to leave the cabbages alone. They are heroes now.

thought: Falador is safe because of them
line: Hello, friend! Falador sleeps soundly, and that is your doing.

thought: gratitude stands, fee paid
line: You have my personal gratitude still, friend, as well as your fee.

thought: nobody else would have thought of a cabbage
line: Nobody else would have thought of a cabbage. Truly, friend, nobody.

thought: points out the vegetable hero to his corgi
line: There goes the one who saved Falador with a vegetable, Sir Burrus.

thought: they'd be first if he knighted freelancers
line: If I made freelancers knights, friend, you would be first. I do not.

thought: they broke only the right thing
line: You broke only what needed breaking, friend. I am most grateful.

thought: almost calls them his agent, corrects himself
line: Ah, our agent! Err... our friend. Simply a friend, naturally.

thought: the realm owes more than the order can pay
line: Asgarnia owes you a debt, friend. The order can scarcely pay it.

thought: the cabbage expert
line: Ah, the cabbage expert. Have you brought any vegetables today?

thought: no knighthood for a cabbage
line: No knighthood for a cabbage, friend. Things are not that dire.

thought: the fee is paid, lingering won't double it
line: The fee has been paid, friend. Lingering will not double it.

thought: saved the city but lost in the castle
line: Saved Falador, and still you cannot find your way out of my castle?

thought: a spy who fights with cabbages
line: A spy who fights with cabbages. Heaven knows what the charter says.

thought: they still smell of cabbage
line: You smell faintly of cabbage still, friend. It may be my imagination.

thought: a squireship might teach them a sword
line: Five years as my squire, friend, and you might learn to use a sword.

thought: honour makes him thank them again, tiresomely
line: Honour obliges me to thank you again. Honour can be very tiresome.

thought: proud of the newest initiate passing
line: Passed every test, our newest initiate. Not many do, what?

thought: selling armour from a bench
line: Initiate armour selling nicely from the bench. Who'd suspect a bench?

thought: waking in Falador beats Lumbridge
line: Wake in Falador's castle, not Lumbridge. The Gaze is a mercy, what?

thought: must talk to Sir Amik about briefings again
line: Must have a word with Sir Amik about briefings. Again, what?

thought: Sir Vey Lance will approve of the new brains
line: Sir Vey Lance will be pleased with the latest one. Brains, at last.

thought: the White Knights can't find his bench
line: White Knights never find this bench, which is rather the point.

thought: glad the order got this one first
line: Brains are wasted in the White Knights. Glad we caught that one first.

thought: a new knight, and nobody may know
line: Spiffing weather for a new knight, what? Not that anyone's to know.

thought: greets his best recruit
line: What ho, old bean! Best recruit we've had in an age, what?

thought: they breezed through the tests
line: Breezed through the tests, old bean. I knew you would, haw haw!

thought: should they die, they'll wake somewhere nicer
line: Should you ever die, old bean, you'll wake in Falador. Much nicer.

thought: they kept their head at the training ground
line: Jolly good show at the training ground. Kept your head, what?

thought: the armour is there when they want it
line: Initiate armour's on the bench whenever you want it, old bean.

thought: one of ours, but hush
line: One of ours now, that one, though nobody's to know it.

thought: a thinking knight pleases Saradomin
line: A thinking knight! Saradomin must be pleased, old bean, and so am I.

thought: the order's pride is a secret too
line: I'd say how proud the order is of you, old bean, but it's a secret.

thought: don't die in the swamp
line: Do try not to die in Lumbridge, old bean. Frightful swamp, what?

thought: a knight who gawps like a sightseer
line: A Temple Knight, and you still gawp at my bench like a sightseer.

thought: too pleased with themselves for a secret knight
line: A secret knight ought to look less pleased with themselves, old bean.

thought: clever enough, only just
line: You squeaked into the Temple Knights, old bean. By a whisker, what?

thought: unbriefed and lucky
line: Unbriefed by Sir Amik, and still you found my bench. Luck, I expect.

thought: looking for the secret ground again
line: Looking for the training ground again, old bean? It's a secret. Shh.

thought: went in unarmed, came out slightly cleverer
line: That one sat the tests empty-handed and came out a little cleverer.

thought: buying armour from a bench, shameless
line: Buying armour off a park bench, old bean? Some knights have no shame.

thought: the best sword waits for a Master
line: The white two-handed sword waits for a Master. It may wait a while.

thought: Adepts are rare enough to celebrate
line: One so seldom sees an Adept. I would shake their hand, I think.

thought: rank is simple arithmetic
line: Black Knights down, rank up. It is a very simple system.

thought: no service for knights who strike their own
line: A knight who strikes down a White Knight will find my counter shut.

thought: a new name on the roll
line: Another name on the roll. The mightiest order in the land grows.

thought: he knows the ranks by heart
line: I could recite every rank in my sleep, from Novice up.

thought: more knights, more ledger
line: The armoury ledger grows with every new knight. So does my headache.

thought: reads a courtyard by its plumes
line: Red plumes, yellow plumes... one eye is enough to read a courtyard.

thought: welcomes a new White Knight to his armoury
line: Ah, one of ours now! Welcome to the armoury, knight.

thought: each Black Knight brings them closer
line: Every Black Knight you fell is a rank closer to Master, knight.

thought: would be glad to serve them at Adept
line: Should you reach Adept, knight, I shall be very glad to serve you.

thought: a keen knight in the armoury, as it should be
line: A White Knight in my armoury, and a keen one. As it should be.

thought: they already walk like a Master
line: You have a Master's walk already, knight. The rest will follow.

thought: the Black Knights will hear of this one
line: There goes a new White Knight. Bad news for the Black Knights.

thought: his father would have liked arming them
line: My father would have been glad to arm a knight like you.

thought: they earn rank the proper way
line: A knight who earns rank the proper way. One does not see enough of it.

thought: no rank, no armour
line: No rank, no armour. The Black Knights will not fell themselves.

thought: he keeps count of their low tally
line: Not many Black Knights felled yet, knight. I keep count, you know.

thought: mind which knights they strike
line: Mind which knights you strike. Ours are the white ones.

thought: baffled that this is a White Knight
line: ... ...you are a White Knight? Well. Standards are not what they were.

thought: hands off the Master's sword
line: Hands off the two-handed sword, knight. That is for Masters.

thought: Sir Amik must have had his reasons
line: Sir Amik knighted you, did he? He must have had his reasons.

thought: talk won't raise their rank
line: Chatter will not raise your rank, knight. Black Knights will.

thought: new, and already eyeing the best
line: A new knight, and already eyeing the Master's rack. Patience, knight.

thought: last of his kind, quietly
line: Last of the Imcando, me. Or so I reckon. Quiet sort of honour.

thought: proud of the copy he made from a portrait
line: Made a knight's sword from a portrait once. Best copy I ever did.

thought: what makes a sword good
line: Iron bars and blurite make a sword. A pie makes it a good one.

thought: the barbarians did for his people
line: Barbarians did for most of my people. Long time ago now.

thought: wonders whether the knight has noticed
line: Wonder if that knight's noticed. Shouldn't think so. Good work, that.

thought: pie got the secret out of him
line: Told a human about my people. Pie loosens a dwarf's tongue, it does.

thought: people want copies, pie first
line: Folk keep asking for that knight's sword. Bring a pie, I tell them.

thought: the ancestors would approve, mostly
line: Ancestors would've been proud of that blade. Well, fairly proud.

thought: greets the pie friend
line: By Guthix, it's my pie friend! Come in out of the wind.

thought: they kept his secret
line: You kept my secret, didn't you? Good. Smiths stick together.

thought: would forge anything for another pie
line: I'd forge a whole armoury for another pie like that, my friend.

thought: few humans know what he is
line: Not many humans know what I am. You're one. Mind that.

thought: pie and listening, rare as Imcando
line: That one brought me pie and listened. Rare as an Imcando, that.

thought: the sword got to the knight thanks to them
line: Fine job, getting that sword back to the knight, my friend.

thought: they've earned a seat by the forge
line: Sit down, my friend. You've earned a seat by my forge.

thought: clever, using pie to find him out
line: Sharp of you, finding an old dwarf out with a pie.

thought: back without pie
line: Back again, and no pie? That's not how we do things now.

thought: don't tell Port Sarim
line: Don't go telling Port Sarim what I am. They'd only want swords.

thought: another sword means bars and pie
line: Another sword? Bring the bars, human, and don't forget the pie.

thought: misattribution: they look like they'd lose a sword
line: You didn't lose that knight's sword yourself? You look the sort.

thought: crumbs on the anvil
line: Pie crumbs on my anvil. That's you, that is. Not that I mind.

thought: no more prying
line: Prying again? I told you about my people. That's your lot.

thought: got past an ice giant, still no smith
line: Fetched blurite past an ice giant, and still you can't swing a hammer.

thought: carrying a pie that badly past an Imcando smith
line: Carry a pie like that past an Imcando smith? You'll drop it.

thought: all that fuss over dye and the village is back where it started
line: All that shouting, all that dye. Goblins back in brown!

thought: goes over the colours that lost, still sore about it
line: Orange clash with skin, blue look silly. So brown win. Hmph.

thought: nothing left to fight about, and boredom is making him desperate
line: Me so bored, me nearly agree with Wartface. Nearly.

thought: eyes Wartface in the new brown and finds the old jibe still works
line: Look at Wartface. New colour, same fat. Colour not problem.

thought: already planning the next argument now the armour is done
line: Next big argue: dinner. Beetle pie or worm stew. Pie win.

thought: the armour quarrel ends and the weapons quarrel begins
line: Armour argue over. Now hammer and axe argue start. Hammer win.

thought: saw Wartface take the brown idea off Grubfoot and claim it
line: Wartface see brown on Grubfoot, then say brown his idea. Ha!

thought: misses having a good colour to bellow
line: Me miss shouting red. Brown not good word for shouting.

thought: the human did what nobody in the hut could: stopped the generals arguing
line: Human stop generals argue. Grubfoot never manage that.

thought: remembers the human brought three lots of armour when asked for one
line: Three armours! Me only ask for one. Human keen.

thought: praises the colour, then takes the credit for it
line: Brown good colour. Me say so first. Human just bring it.

thought: the whole village matches now, and he knows who did it
line: Village look proper now, all same colour. Human do that.

thought: bored since the armour was settled, glad of something new to look at
line: Human back! Good. Me bored since armour. Human interesting.

thought: points the human out to Wartface as proof somebody has a brain
line: Look, Wartface! Armour fixer back. That one got brain.

thought: the highest honour he can think of: a small general's post, under him
line: Human could be general, maybe. Small general. Under me.

thought: offers to share the dinner he never lets Wartface near
line: Human want beetle pie? Me share. Me not share with Wartface.

thought: the human went all over for dye and came back with the old colour
line: Human run about whole land for dye, and bring back brown. Ha!

thought: still haunted by the first colour the human tried
line: Human bring orange first. Orange! Goblin look like rotten fruit.

thought: the human settled the argument and took his favourite pastime with it
line: Human take away good argue. Now me bored. Human fault.

thought: brown was right there all along; a small goblin could have picked it
line: Human think long, bring brown. Grubfoot could do that.

thought: the job is done, so why is the human still standing in the hut
line: Armour done. Human still hang about? Generals got shouting to do.

thought: the human might want thanks; goblins don't do thanks, goblins win
line: Human want thank you? Goblins not say thank you. Goblins win.

thought: blue was the silliest of the lot; he looked bruised in it
line: Blue, human? Me in blue look like one big bruise.

thought: warns Wartface that the dye-fetcher is back and might start again
line: Wartface, look. Brown-fetcher back. Hide dye!

thought: seven elders voted, and he named a new Fremennik himself
line: Seven elders voted! It is not every winter I name a new one.

thought: thinking of the other one who came from outside and passed the trials
line: Koschei passed his trials too. I still fear he will remember and go.

thought: a new name to call at the feast, and he means to get it right
line: Another name to call at the feast. I shall get it right, mostly.

thought: the Moon Clan would have tried it with spells; this one did it the hard way
line: The Moon Clan would cheat the trials with spells. Ours sweat for it.

thought: even the newest of his people sneaks a look at the helm
line: Even our newest Fremennik eyes my helm. Some things never change.

thought: next time someone calls them barbarians, there is one more to answer
line: Call us barbarians now, and one more of us will answer back.

thought: the council argued and voted and drank, in good order for once
line: The council argued, voted, and drank. In that order, for once.

thought: all men were Fremennik once, so a newcomer can be kin come home
line: Every so often, a stranger turns out to be kin. It is good to see.

thought: the newcomer walks his hall as one of the tribe now
line: Well met! You walk my hall like you were born to it now.

thought: he gave the name himself, and is proud of his choice
line: The name I gave you suits you. I am rarely wrong about names.

thought: calls for a cup for the newest member of the tribe
line: Our newest Fremennik! Fill a cup for them, someone.

thought: the law asks seven votes of twelve; he'd have given all of them
line: Seven of twelve, the law says. I would have given you all twelve.

thought: most of his people were born to what this one fought for
line: You earned what most of my people were simply handed at birth.

thought: offers the hospitality of the longhall, with a warning about the kegs
line: My hall is your hall now. Do not drink it dry.

thought: some elders like nobody, and this one won them anyway
line: Hah! The one who won over seven elders. Some of them like nobody.

thought: a warrior he'd want at his back in a fight
line: If I needed a warrior at my back tonight, I would call for you.

thought: one of the tribe now, and still drinks like a polite guest
line: Fremennik now, and still you sip your beer like a guest.

thought: the new name mustn't swell the head; there's no room in his helm
line: Do not let the name go to your head. My helm barely fits as it is.

thought: the council has argued about that vote ever since
line: Seven votes, and the council has argued about them ever since.
