thought: he gave a Fremennik name; now it has to be lived up to
line: I gave you a Fremennik name. Do try to live up to it.

thought: suspects some elders only voted to spite the others
line: Half the council voted for you to make the other half cross.

thought: the newest of the tribe makes straight for the kegs, as a Fremennik should
line: Watch our newest, straight for the kegs. Fremennik already, that one.

thought: one of the tribe means one of those who clear up after the feast
line: You are one of us now, which means you clean up after the feast.

thought: the newcomer still eyes his helm as though it might bite
line: Still you look at my helm as though it might bite. It has.

thought: he blessed that traveller and saw something of the faith there
line: There is something of the faith in that traveller. I am rarely wrong.

thought: keeps the swamp's old name alive in his prayers
line: Humblethorn, they called it, before the rot. I say the name in prayer.

thought: prays for the travellers out in Mort Myre tonight
line: I pray the ghasts go hungry tonight. Travellers too often do.

thought: mud on the clean floor again, and he knows where from
line: Mud on my clean floor again. Mort Myre mud, by the smell.

thought: a Guthixian would call the swamp balance; he calls it rot
line: Guthixians would call that swamp balance. I call it rot.

thought: he suggested a life in the faith and got only a smile
line: I suggested a life of service to that one. I got a smile.

thought: the pass is quiet tonight and he likes it that way
line: The pass into Morytania is quiet tonight. I prefer it so.

thought: the Seven fought ten days unsleeping; he nods off in his prayers
line: The Seven fought ten days without sleep. I nod off at my prayers.

thought: he still sees the touch of faith he blessed in this one
line: There is something of the faith about you, friend. I mean it kindly.

thought: they went into the swamp and came out still themselves
line: You walked into Mort Myre and came out still yourself. Bless you.

thought: wonders if the player has thought about serving Saradomin
line: Have you thought on what I said? Saradomin could use you, friend.

thought: the ghasts never got their food, or them
line: The ghasts never got your supper, I see. Or you.

thought: blesses every traveller, and this one gets it twice
line: I bless every traveller who passes. You, I bless twice.

thought: good work done in that swamp, seen above and here
line: Few would do good work in that swamp. Saradomin noticed, and so did I.

thought: could picture this one in a priest's robes
line: There goes one I would gladly see in the robes of a priest.

thought: offers them a friend at the temple, whatever comes
line: You have a friend at Paterdomus, whatever the road brings.

thought: he did say something of the faith; a small something
line: I said there was something of the faith in you. A small something.

thought: the player brings the swamp in on their boots
line: You track half of Mort Myre into my temple every visit.

thought: offered a life of service, got a face like gruel
line: A life of service, I suggested. You looked as if I offered gruel.

thought: the ghasts must not have wanted them
line: The ghasts must have found you too tough to bother with.

thought: Saradomin forgives, but the swamp smell is another matter
line: Saradomin forgives much, friend. The swamp smell may take longer.

thought: would make a fine priest if they ever stopped moving
line: You'd make a fine priest, if you ever sat still long enough.

thought: feared that much time in the swamp would turn them Guthixian
line: Out in that swamp so long, I feared you'd come back a Guthixian.

thought: smelt them before seeing them
line: Ah, our swamp-walker! I smelt you before I saw you.

thought: no plague at all, so what are the mourners for
line: No plague at all. So what have the mourners been doing over there?

thought: Guidor's tests were clean, which means someone lied
line: Guidor's tests came back clean. Someone's been lying, and loudly.

thought: the king built the wall, so the king knows
line: The king had that wall built. He knows why, even if I don't.

thought: her mother wants her to stop fretting
line: Mother wants me to stop worrying now. As if worry works like that.

thought: a secret was the answer she got, and secrets started all this
line: A secret, I'm told. Secrets are how this whole mess started.

thought: a quiet day of small hurts for once
line: Quiet day. A burn and a splinter. I could get used to quiet.

thought: who would bother inventing a plague
line: Who invents a plague? Honestly, the trouble it must take.

thought: means to write to her old teacher tonight
line: I'll write to Guidor tonight. He'll want to know I'm still at it.

thought: the player got her sample to Guidor safely
line: Hey! Thanks again for getting my sample to Guidor in one piece.

thought: cross about the secret, but respects that they kept their word
line: You kept the king's secret. I'm cross, but I do respect it.

thought: a healer's eye: they look well after all that running
line: You look well. After all that running about, I'm amazed.

thought: they went to the king on her account
line: You went to the king for me. Not many would knock on that door.

thought: someone around here actually finishes what they start
line: Someone round here actually finishes what they start. Nice change.

thought: offers free patching up, any time
line: If you ever need patching up, come to me first. No charge.

thought: worries a little less when this one is about
line: I worry less with you about. Only a little less, mind.

thought: points out the one who helped show there was no plague
line: There's the one who helped prove there's no plague. Well, half.

thought: they won't tell her what the king said, so she'll guess
line: You won't tell me what the king said. Fine. I'll guess, loudly.

thought: carried a sample all that way without dropping it, a miracle
line: All that way with my sample and you didn't drop it. Miracles happen.

thought: went all the way to the king and came back with nothing to say
line: All the way to the king, and back with nothing to tell me?

thought: fewer bruises next time, please; bandages don't grow on trees
line: Do try to come back with fewer bruises. I've only so many bandages.

thought: they look like they've been running errands for everyone again
line: You look like you've been running errands for everyone. Again.

thought: somebody else must need a parcel carried
line: Somebody else need a parcel carried? You've the look.

thought: points out the one who keeps royal secrets from a healer
line: Look who it is. The one who keeps royal secrets from healers.

thought: no plague means no excuse for staying away from the other side
line: No plague, so no excuse to stay out of West Ardougne now.

thought: the Grail is at Camelot and he can't stop admiring it
line: The Grail, here at Camelot! I keep going to look at it.

thought: young Percival, a king now
line: King Percival! Young Percival, a king. I can hardly believe it.

thought: Lancelot doubted a commoner could do it, and has gone quiet
line: Lancelot's very quiet about the Grail. Very quiet indeed.

thought: the dead land bloomed the moment Percival took the throne
line: Percival took his throne and the whole land bloomed. Imagine!

thought: already wondering about the next quest
line: Now, what's the next quest? There's always a next quest.

thought: came from another world and found the Grail in this one
line: We came from afar, and the Grail was here all along. Fancy that!

thought: keeps moving the Grail to find its best spot
line: I've moved the Grail twice today. It looks best by the window.

thought: wonders how to send word to a king in the Fisher Realm
line: Must write to Percival. Do kings of the Fisher Realm get letters?

thought: the knight who brought the Grail home
line: Welcome back, brave knight! The Grail's home, thanks to you.

thought: calls Merlin to see the Grail-finder
line: Merlin, look! Our Grail-finder's back!

thought: found what the whole Round Table couldn't
line: You found what my whole Round Table couldn't. I shan't forget it.

thought: Percival's crown and his green land came through this knight
line: Percival owes you his crown, my knight. So does his whole land.

thought: the finest quester at Camelot, but Lancelot mustn't hear it

thought: chatter belongs in Varrock
line: Want chatter? Varrock's down the road, not here.

thought: he'll believe it when he sees a dragon's head
line: Fancy-pants hero, are we? I'll believe it when I see a dragon's head.

thought: prove something before staring at his hut
line: Go prove something first, then come and stare at my hut.

thought: needs more than talk to wear his plate
line: You'd need more than talk to wear my plate. A dragon, say.

thought: told them: dragon first, then platemail
line: Told 'em: slay the dragon of Crandor, then we'll talk platemail.

thought: quiet now they've gone dragon-hunting
line: 'Tis quiet now they've gone dragon-hunting. Long may it last.

thought: wonders if they've been eaten
line: Wonder if that last one's been eaten yet.

thought: dragon questions go to the Guildmaster
line: Guildmaster can answer the dragon questions. Not me.

thought: platebody polished and waiting, maybe long
line: Platebody's polished and waiting. Might wait a long while.

thought: he isn't hard, just particular
line: Folk think I'm hard. I just like me armour on folk who've earned it.

thought: a dragon for a platebody is fair
line: A dragon for a platebody. Fair trade, by my reckoning.

thought: he'll eat his words if they return
line: If they come back wi' the dragon slain, I'll eat my words.

thought: still alive; Crandor hasn't had them
line: Still in one piece? Crandor hasn't had you yet, then.

thought: they took it on
line: You went and took it on. Didn't think ye would.

thought: more spine than most
line: More spine on that one than most the Guildmaster sends.

thought: a hero in them yet, maybe
line: Aye, there might be a hero in you yet. Might.

thought: not run off yet
line: Not run off yet. That's sommat.

thought: keep their head; platebody waits
line: Keep yer head on, adventurer. Platebody's waiting.

thought: they look like they have a plan
line: You've the look of someone with a plan. First one I've seen.

thought: less swagger since the dragon was mentioned
line: Bit less swagger on you since I mentioned that dragon. Good.

thought: the dragon is on Crandor, not here
line: Dragon's on Crandor, not in Edgeville. Ye might've noticed.

thought: back already, lost nerve
line: Back already? Lost your nerve, have you?

thought: staring won't change the terms
line: No platebody till the dragon's dead. Staring won't change that.

thought: not their nursemaid
line: Ask the Guildmaster how to kill it. I'm not yer nursemaid.

thought: alive, so not been to Crandor
line: Still alive, so ye've not been to Crandor yet.

thought: all talk and no dragon
line: All talk and no dragon, adventurer. Same as the rest.

thought: that face won't scare a dragon
line: Ye'll need more than that face to scare off a dragon.

thought: cold feet
line: Cold feet, is it? Crandor's not getting any closer.

thought: Wartface stands right there, and calling him fat is the best sport in the hut
line: Wartface fat. Me not tell him quiet. Me tell him loud.

thought: smells the cook's pot and it's for the other general again
line: Mudknuckles make worm stew for Wartface. Who make pie for me?

thought: his dinner was plain maggot again, no spice
line: Plain maggot taste of nothing. Need spice. Need fruit!

thought: thinks of the goblin who got caught
line: Wormbrain steal one time too many. Now he sit in Port Sarim jail.

thought: his plan for the army, heavy and simple
line: Every soldier get big warhammer. Bonk! Fight over.

thought: goblins never lose, by his reckoning
line: Goblins always win. Even when goblins lose, goblins win.

thought: tells the old legend the way he likes it
line: Old story say Dorgesh tribe run from fight. God shut them in ground.

thought: can't find the puzzle box he hands to treasure hunters
line: Where me put puzzle box? Wartface sit on it, probably.

thought: a human who isn't as fat as Wartface is already ahead
line: Human not as fat as Wartface. That good start, human.

thought: wants someone to agree with him; decides this one does
line: You look like you agree with me, human. Clever human.

thought: the stranger walked past Wartface without laughing
line: Human walk past Wartface and not laugh. Good manners, that.

thought: a strong arm is good for one thing: a big lump of iron
line: Strong arms on this human. Could swing proper warhammer, maybe.

thought: praise that is really a dig at Wartface
line: Ha! Human smarter than Wartface. Not hard, but still.

thought: greets them the goblin way, not the wimpy old way
line: Me give human victory salute. Not silly bow like Wartface do.

thought: assumes anyone from the big world knows his tribe's colour wins
line: Human come from big world. Human know red best colour, yes?

thought: the human hasn't asked anything daft yet
line: Not one stupid question from human yet. Best human all day.

thought: a human wanders into the generals' hut while he is busy being right
line: What human want? Me in middle of being right.

thought: ugly, but at least not Wartface-ugly
line: Human uglier than Wartface. Nearly. Wartface still win.

thought: the human hanging about reminds him of the smallest goblin
line: Human follow me about like Grubfoot. Me not need two Grubfoots.

thought: humans have no tribe and no tribe colour
line: No tribe, no colour. Human just walk about any old how.

thought: the face looks like it is having its first thought
line: Wartface! Look at this one. Nearly ugly as Wartface!

thought: decides the human is about to do the old tribal bow
line: Human going to bow? Bow make goblin look wimp. Human too.

thought: there's a whiff of the other general's dinner about
line: Human smell like worm stew. That Wartface fault, probably.

thought: a stranger with no hammer and no sense
line: Me seen cleverer rocks, human. Rocks not wander into hut.

thought: the new century is coming and he wants red for it
line: New century coming. New armour. Red armour, if Wartface see sense.

thought: plain brown armour bores him to sleep
line: Brown armour so boring. Me fall asleep looking at it.

thought: Wartface keeps pushing green
line: Green? Green make goblin look like no armour at all!

thought: gloats that half the village still wears his red
line: Wartface say goblins listen to him. Half village in red! Ha!

thought: he will just keep saying it
line: Red. Red. Red. Me say it till Wartface go deaf.

thought: the old battle deserves new armour
line: Plain of Mud big day for goblins. Need big new armour for it.

thought: they argued all morning and nobody won
line: Argue all morning. Argue all afternoon. Nobody win.

thought: his tribe wore red in the old days
line: Thorobshuun wear red in old days. Old days best days.

thought: guesses the stranger is on his side
line: Human! You look like you think red best. Me can tell.

thought: Wartface hates clever things, so a clever face pleases him
line: Wartface, see this one? Clever. Wartface hate clever.

thought: the stranger hasn't had to listen to Wartface for years yet
line: Lucky human. Not sick of Wartface yet. Me jealous.

thought: the human is standing on his side of the hut
line: Good human stand on my side of hut. Wartface side smell.

thought: someone turns up just before the new century
line: Human come just in time for goblin new century. Smart human.

thought: a big strong human must know a hammer beats an axe
line: Big strong human. Human know hammer beat axe, yes?

thought: at least this one has an opinion, unlike Grubfoot
line: Human got opinion, me can tell. Better than Grubfoot.

thought: would rather look at the human than at Wartface
line: Nice to look at something not Wartface. Even human.

thought: armour business is for generals; the human can go stand with the runt
line: Armour talk for generals. Human go stand by Grubfoot.

thought: a human who can't tell red from green belongs with Wartface
line: Human not know red from green? Go sit with Wartface, then.

thought: a human has wandered into the general hut
line: Human wander into general hut. Big mistake, little human.

thought: humans don't get a say in goblin colours
line: Human want vote on colour? Human not goblin. No vote.

thought: the human has never heard of the goblin new century
line: You not even know about goblin new century? Silly human.

thought: why is the human looking at him when Wartface is right there
line: Why human look at me? Look at Wartface. Much funnier.

thought: gets the fat jibe in sideways
line: Human fat? No. Wartface fat. Human just ugly.

thought: calls the runt over, as the stranger has wandered in
line: Grubfoot! Who let this one in? Shut up, Grubfoot. Me know.

thought: the human has gone for armour and he hopes hard
line: Human bring armour soon. Red armour, me hope. Me hope very hard.

thought: he has no idea where dye comes from and doesn't care
line: Where dye come from? Me not know. Me general, not dye goblin.

thought: the spare armour is in a crate nobody can name
line: Wartface say spare armour in crate. Which crate? He not know!

thought: the stranger does the colour job while he does the important one
line: Human do colour job. Me do important job. Shouting.

thought: if it comes back green he'd rather go without
line: Green armour? Me rather wear nothing. Look same anyway.

thought: Wartface's witch story sounds made up to him
line: Draynor witch? Wartface make that up. Me sure.

thought: time is running short before the celebration
line: New century nearly here, and armour still not done!

thought: he sent the human north to find dye and they came back
line: Me tell human go north for dye. Human come back! Good, maybe.

thought: the human is running errands for goblins
line: Human run about for goblins! Human good runner.

thought: faster than the smallest goblin, which isn't hard
line: Human fetch armour quicker than Grubfoot. Grubfoot slow.

thought: hopes the helper is on the red side
line: Human help with colour. Human know red best, yes?

thought: praise that corrects itself into a dig
line: Human cleverer than both generals. No. Than Wartface.

thought: the best reward he can think of is his own unwanted stew
line: Good human. Me tell Mudknuckles give you worm stew. Me not want it.

thought: the War God might notice someone working this hard
line: Human work hard for goblins. Me might even remember human name.

thought: most humans would have given up by now
line: Human not give up yet. Most humans soft. Not you.

thought: shows the helper off to the rival general
line: Wartface, see? This one work hard. Me pick good one.

thought: the new century will be over at this rate
line: Human take long time. Goblin new century be over soon.

thought: he thought of red straight away; why can't the human
line: Human think of colour yet? Me think of red. Easy.

thought: the human looks lost, and he's no help with directions
line: Human look lost. Dye that way, maybe. Or that way.

thought: humans are good at fetching and carrying
line: Human fetch and carry for goblins. Human good at that.

thought: choosing this human proves Wartface is stupid
line: Wartface pick this one for job. Shows how stupid Wartface is.

thought: slow, like Wartface after a big bowl of worm stew
line: Slow human. Slow like Wartface after worm stew.

thought: if the colour comes back wrong it gets thrown
line: Bring wrong colour, human, and me throw it at you. Then Wartface.

thought: hasn't found the right dye, which he couldn't find either
line: Still no dye, human? Me not find it either. But me general.

thought: Bentnoze in his red looks like a vegetable
line: Bentnoze in red look like big tomato. Me say nothing. Me just look.

thought: thinks of a proper dinner
line: Juicy maggot. Soggy bread. That proper dinner.

thought: preaches about the War God, pompously
line: Without Big High War God, goblin just small green thing.

thought: can't remember where the spare armour went
line: Which crate spare armour in? Me knew yesterday.

thought: axes against hammers, again
line: Battleaxe sharp. Warhammer only good for nails. Me right again.

thought: concedes he could manage peace, on terms
line: Me could do peace. Peace in green, though.

thought: Grubfoot is about to say something
line: Grubfoot open mouth again. Shut up, Grubfoot.

thought: proud of whatever goblin nicked the dye
line: Some goblin steal dye off old witch in Draynor. Good goblin.

thought: the human is ugly but less ugly than the usual run
line: Human less ugly than most humans. Still ugly. But less.

thought: decides the human must be green at heart
line: Human got Garagorshuun heart, maybe. Green heart.

thought: the human isn't standing with Bentnoze
line: You not stand with Bentnoze? Clever human.

thought: walks like a warrior, which the War God would like
line: Human walk like warrior. Big High War God like that.

thought: a sharp look, like an axe, not a hammer
line: Sharp look on this human. Like battleaxe, not silly hammer.

thought: Bentnoze has never been right, so the opposite must be true
line: Bentnoze call this one stupid. Bentnoze never right. So, clever!

thought: knows when to keep quiet, unlike the runt
line: Human know when to shut up. Better than Grubfoot.

thought: praise measured in his favourite food
line: Me like human. Nearly much as juicy maggot.

thought: the human compares poorly with a maggot
line: Me seen prettier maggot. Juicy one, too.

thought: walked past the bigger general without a word
line: Human walk past big general and not even look. Rude human.

thought: humans have no tribe to speak of
line: Human got no tribe. Human just... human. Sad.

thought: the human looks like they'd side with Bentnoze
line: Human look like Bentnoze friend. Bad thing to look like.

thought: even Bentnoze could win that fight
line: Bentnoze could beat human in fight. Bentnoze! Think on that.

thought: humans are like bread: too crunchy
line: Human crunchy like bread. Goblin not like crunchy.

thought: the War God made goblins strong and humans otherwise
line: Big High War God use up all strong on goblins. Human get leftovers.

thought: sends the runt for a bucket
line: Grubfoot, fetch bucket. This one ugly enough to scare maggots.

thought: the new century needs new armour and the answer is obvious
line: New century need new armour. Green armour. Easy choice.

thought: the village listens to him because he is bigger
line: Village listen to me. Me bigger general. Shut up, Bentnoze.

thought: brown is dull as mud
line: Brown armour dull as mud. Goblin need green for new century.

thought: his tribe's green against Bentnoze's tribe
line: Garagorshuun always wear green. Thorobshuun rubbish.

thought: he has thought about it very hard
line: Me think. Me think hard. Still green.

thought: a village in red would look like a human village
line: Whole village in red? Ugly! Not happen while me general.

thought: peace with Bentnoze, on his terms
line: Peace with Bentnoze? Maybe. If Bentnoze wear green.

thought: the War God surely wants green for the Plain of Mud day
line: Plain of Mud day coming. Big High War God want green, me sure.

thought: the human isn't standing next to Bentnoze
line: Human got sense. Human not stand next to Bentnoze.

thought: looks like the sort who knows green is best
line: You look like human who know green best. Good human.

thought: the human doesn't argue, unlike Bentnoze
line: Me like human. Human not argue. Bentnoze always argue.

thought: walks in like a general, second biggest
line: Human walk in like big general. Second biggest. After me.

thought: has ears, so can listen to the bigger general
line: Good ears on this human. Good for listen to bigger general.

thought: no smell of beetle pie about this one
line: Human not smell of beetle pie. Big point for human.

thought: tells Grubfoot off to talk to the human
line: Shut up, Grubfoot, me talk to human. Human more interesting.

thought: notices the stranger stopped on his half of the hut
line: Ha! This one stand on green side of hut. Clever one.

thought: the human is as ugly as a village in red
line: Look, Bentnoze. This one ugly as whole village in red.

thought: thinks the human believes Bentnoze is the bigger general
line: Human think Bentnoze bigger general? Human wrong. Human ugly too.

thought: humans know nothing of the goblin new century
line: Human know nothing about goblin new century. Only human things.

thought: goblins are bad at peace, humans worse
line: Goblins bad at peace. Humans worse. You worst, probably.

thought: who let the human in? probably the runt
line: Who let human in hut? Grubfoot? Shut up, Grubfoot.

thought: a human who likes brown is as boring as Bentnoze
line: Human like brown armour? Human boring as Bentnoze.

thought: compares the human to a sad, dry maggot
line: Human look like dry maggot. Not juicy one, either.

thought: the human hammers on about nothing, like Bentnoze's hammers
line: Human brain like warhammer. Only good for nails.

thought: waiting for the armour, which he is bad at
line: Armour coming soon. Me not good at wait.

thought: the dye came from a witch, and could come again
line: Need more dye? Goblin nick it off Draynor witch before. Do it again!

thought: spare armour is in a crate, somewhere
line: Spare armour in crate somewhere. Me forget which. Not important.

thought: if it comes back green he'll wear it all century
line: If armour come green, me wear it whole new century.

thought: Bentnoze is already practising saying red, so he'll be louder
line: Bentnoze practise saying red. Me practise saying green. Louder.

thought: Grubfoot wants a say in the colour
line: Grubfoot want pick colour. Shut up, Grubfoot. Generals decide.

thought: a quick word upward
line: Big High War God watching. Him make it green. Me sure.

thought: bigger general gets to try the new armour first
line: Me bigger general, so me try armour first. Fair.

thought: the human is working for goblins, which is right
line: Human work for goblins! Good. Work for green side most.

thought: quick on their feet, like a hungry maggot
line: Human quick on feet. Quick like hungry maggot.

thought: faster than the goblin who stole the dye
line: Human find dye faster than goblin who steal it off witch.

thought: admits, once, that the human is useful
line: Human useful. Me not say that often. Me not say it again.

thought: not frightened of the general hut
line: Human not scared of general hut. Brave, for human.

thought: he's the bigger general so his judgement counts
line: You do good job. Me bigger general. Me know good job.

thought: points the helper out to Grubfoot as an example
line: Grubfoot, watch this one. That how goblin carry armour. Nearly.

thought: told the village about the helper; they didn't believe it
line: Me tell village human help goblins. Village laugh. Me not laugh.

thought: the human is taking ages
line: Human take long time. Maggot grow up faster.

thought: red armour would get the human thrown out
line: Bring wrong colour, human, and out of hut you go. Head first.

thought: asking Bentnoze about dye is a mistake
line: Human ask Bentnoze where dye come from? Ha! Bentnoze not know!

thought: a big job for a small human
line: Big job for small human. Me not hopeful.

thought: the human thinks they get to choose the colour
line: Human think human choose colour? Ha! Generals choose.

thought: slow as Bentnoze picking fruit out of his dinner
line: Human slow as Bentnoze eating fruit. Very slow.

thought: helping both generals makes them two-faced
line: Human help both generals? Two-faced human. Both faces ugly.

thought: fetching and carrying is a human job; shouting is a goblin's
line: Bentnoze, look. This one fetch, we shout. Good system.

thought: he keeps the memory of the Seven where they fell
line: It is said seven priests held this ground for ten days and nights.

thought: the blessing on the river is what keeps the dark out
line: Every morning I pray the blessing on the Salve holds.

thought: the swamp was a forest once
line: Hard to believe that swamp was ever a lovely forest. Yet it was.

thought: thinks fondly of the druid who leads lost travellers out
line: I believe Filliman quietly leads lost travellers out of that swamp.

thought: Guthixians and their claims tire him
line: Guthixians make a great many claims. Few bear looking into.

thought: the warning he gives every traveller about ghasts
line: The ghasts take your food first, and then they take you.

thought: the temple guards the only way east
line: This temple stands at the only pass into Morytania. I never forget it.

thought: most of a priest's day is humbler than people think
line: A priest's work is mostly prayer and sweeping. Mostly sweeping.

thought: a blessing for anyone heading east
line: Saradomin keep you, adventurer. The road east is not a kind one.

thought: the traveller seems calm, which is rare near Morytania
line: You have a steady way about you, adventurer. That is rare here.

thought: the Seven would have had room for one more
line: I think the Seven would have found room for one like you.

thought: it heartens him to see someone still walking upright this close to the river
line: It does my heart good to see a traveller still walking upright.

thought: few come near the Salve by choice
line: Not many come this near the Salve on purpose. Good for you.

thought: walks as if they had somewhere good to be
line: You walk as though you have somewhere good to be. I envy that.

thought: a priest's quiet approval of decent folk
line: Travellers who pass this way are braver than they know.

thought: he will pray for this one gladly
line: I shall remember you in my prayers tonight, adventurer.

thought: adventurers poke about old temples looking for treasure
line: Adventurers do love to poke about old temples. Please do not.

thought: suspects a Guthixian, politely
line: You'd not be a Guthixian, would you? You have that look.

thought: the sort who'd dig up holy dead for a trinket
line: Forgive me, but you look like one who'd dig up a tomb for a trinket.

thought: crossing into Morytania without a prayer
line: Crossing into Morytania without a prayer? How very brave.

thought: a little more faith, a little less swagger
line: Another adventurer with more swagger than faith. Saradomin help us.

thought: the ghasts would make short work of this one
line: I fear the ghasts would find you a very easy meal.

thought: looks like someone who skips their prayers
line: You have the air of one who skips prayers. I shall pray for two.

thought: adventurers always want proof
line: Proof, proof. Adventurers always want proof. Faith asks less.

thought: the coffin beside his cell troubles his nights
line: The lid moved in the night, I am sure of it. Or I dreamt it.

thought: locked up in his own temple by Zamorakians
line: Locked in my own temple, by Zamorakians. Saradomin grant me patience.

thought: his blood is the sort a vampyre would know
line: A vampyre would know my blood. I try very hard not to dwell on it.

thought: they left him the coffin for company
line: They locked me in and left me a coffin for company.

thought: the Seven held ten days; he can hold a few more
line: The Seven held for ten days and nights. I can hold a little longer.

thought: prays at the bars; the coffin does not join in
line: I pray at these bars each night. The coffin does not pray back.

thought: Zamorakians in a house of Saradomin
line: Zamorakians in a house of Saradomin. It turns my stomach.

thought: the view from the top of the temple is all he has
line: Such a fine view from up here. I would trade it for a door.

thought: someone has finally come; his prayers were heard
line: You came! Saradomin heard me after all, adventurer.

thought: grateful to anyone who'd climb up to a forgotten prisoner
line: Bless you for climbing all this way to a forgotten prisoner.

thought: they walked right past the Zamorakians to get here
line: It took a brave heart to walk past those Zamorakians.

thought: a friendly face after so long
line: A friendly face, at last! I had nearly forgotten what one looked like.

thought: frets over the stairs, because he needs his rescuer whole
line: Mind the stairs, my rescuer. I need you in one piece.

thought: the timing is a small miracle
line: Your timing, adventurer, is a small miracle.

thought: can see goodness in them from behind the bars
line: There is good in you, adventurer. I can see it even from in here.

thought: Saradomin chose well
line: Saradomin chose well when he sent you up those stairs.

thought: the rescuer took their time getting here
line: Did you stop for a bite on the way up? I did wonder.

thought: adventurers always want to look in the coffin
line: You'll want a peek in the coffin, I suppose. Adventurers always do.

thought: prayed for a hero and got this one
line: I prayed for a hero. Saradomin, it seems, has a sense of humour.

thought: not quite sure whose side they're on
line: Forgive me, but are you quite sure which side you are on?

thought: no hurry, he only has a vampyre for company
line: Oh, take your time. I have only a vampyre for company.

thought: they look the sort the Zamorakians would hire
line: You look rather like the sort those Zamorakians would hire.

thought: the rescuer's breathing might wake the coffin
line: Do stand back from the coffin. Your breathing might wake it.

thought: a polite reminder that he is still in here
line: Still here, adventurer. Still locked in. In case you wondered.

thought: the Salve runs clean again and he keeps it that way
line: The Salve runs clean again. I bless it every morning, to be sure.

thought: his druid friend never comes by now
line: I set a place for Filliman some evenings. He never comes now.

thought: lost wolfbane daggers wash up on the riverbank
line: Wolfbane daggers wash up on the banks now and then. Lost, poor things.

thought: Veliaf is an old friend, gruff but good
line: Veliaf is an old friend of mine. Gruff, but his heart is sound.

thought: urges travellers to listen for the Myreque
line: If you hear talk of the Myreque, do listen. They are good people.

thought: still offended that anyone would foul a holy river
line: Zamorakians fouling a holy river. Whatever next, I wonder.

thought: nobody will foul that well again
line: That well will not be fouled again while I draw breath.

thought: worries the druid isn't looking after himself
line: Is Filliman eating, out there? Druids do forget.

thought: this is the one who saved the temple
line: Ah, my friend! You saved this temple, and I have not forgotten.

thought: the family dagger went to the right hands
line: Keep my family's dagger close, friend. You earned it.

thought: the Salve owes them its blessing
line: The Salve owes you its blessing, friend. So do I.

thought: he sleeps again, thanks to them
line: I sleep soundly again, thanks to you. Well, mostly.

thought: they carried the essence as if the faith depended on it
line: You carried that essence as if the faith depended on it. It did.

thought: Veliaf would approve, and he approves of few
line: Veliaf would like you, I think. He likes very few.

thought: they are always welcome at the temple
line: You will always be welcome at Paterdomus, my friend.

thought: his nightly prayers for them seem to be working
line: I have prayed for you every night since. It seems to be working.

thought: there is still essence dust on the altar
line: My friend, you left essence dust on the altar. Saradomin forgives.

thought: hopes the wolfbane won't end up in the river
line: Still carrying my wolfbane? Do try not to drop it in the river.

thought: something always needs blessing after a visit from them
line: Every time you visit, something needs blessing afterwards.

thought: they haven't been to a single service
line: I trust you've been to a service since? No. I thought not.

thought: heroes are never tidy
line: Heroes are rarely tidy, I find. You are no exception.

thought: the temple saviour is back, and so is the mess
line: Someone fetch a broom. The saviour of Paterdomus is back.

thought: Veliaf has no patience for dawdlers
line: Never let Veliaf see you dawdle like that. He has no patience for it.

thought: saved the temple, then walked straight past the altar
line: Saved the temple, and still you walk past the altar. Tsk.

thought: never wanted to lead anyone
line: Never asked to lead anyone. The others just started looking at me.

thought: being called an organisation is a joke to him
line: Someone called us an organisation once. I laughed for a week.

thought: the rule he gives everyone near vampyres
line: Silver and garlic. Never go near a vampyre without both.

thought: why he fights, said flatly
line: They took everyone I cared about. I don't intend to stop.

thought: a soldier's prayer for the ones still standing
line: Saradomin watch over the ones still standing.

thought: between the swamp and the towns there's no safe choice
line: Ghasts in the swamp, vampyres in the towns. Some choice.

thought: Drezel keeps faith at the temple
line: Drezel keeps the faith at Paterdomus. Someone has to.

thought: a quiet day counts as a good one here
line: Quiet day. In Morytania, that counts as a good one.

thought: this one looks like they'd hold a blade steady
line: Well met, friend. You look like you could hold a blade steady.

thought: not bitten yet, which is something

line: One more adventurer asking to fight our warriors, and I shall retire.

line: If you have come to complain of the heat, the gate is that way.

thought: aside to a guard: watch that one near the windows, politely
line: Do watch that one near the windows. Discreetly, of course.

thought: they strike him as a person who climbs things
line: With respect, you strike me as a person who climbs things.

thought: the accounts balance, unlike their manners
line: The accounts balance, which is more than I can say for your manners.

thought: they're loitering somewhere unsuitable near the palace
line: Kindly stand somewhere a little less... adventurous.

thought: the palace tiptoes about since the prince was taken
line: Our prince taken, and the whole palace walking on eggshells.

thought: he needs someone reliable, not a show-off
line: I need someone who can get a job done. Not a hero. Someone reliable.

thought: Osman has methods Hassan prefers not to know
line: Osman has his methods. I have learnt not to ask what they are.

thought: how to tell the Emir there's still no news
line: How does one tell the Emir that his son is still not found?

thought: the accounts can wait, the prince can't
line: The accounts can wait. The prince cannot.

thought: every courtier has a theory, none a plan
line: Every courtier has a theory, and not one of them has a plan.

thought: the palace feels quiet without the prince
line: A palace without its prince is a very quiet place.

thought: Osman counsels patience but Hassan has to answer for it
line: Osman counsels patience. Osman does not have to run the palace.

thought: they look capable, which matters these days
line: You have a capable look about you. These days, that is worth noticing.

thought: aside to a guard: there goes someone who looks like they finish things
line: There goes someone who looks as though they finish what they begin.

thought: they seem the dependable sort, which the palace lacks
line: If I may say so, you seem the dependable sort. We could use one.

thought: someone with purpose in their stride; the city needs that now
line: Ah. Purpose in your stride. Al Kharid has need of that just now.

thought: the Emir values those who see things through
line: The Emir values people who see things through. You look one such.

thought: in dark days a steady face is welcome
line: Welcome, traveller. In darker days, a steady face is a comfort.

thought: they've travelled far and kept their head
line: Travelled far, I think, and kept your head. Admirable.

thought: he apologises for staring; he's always looking for capable people now
line: Forgive my staring. I am always looking for capable people these days.

thought: the palace needs someone capable; don't take it personally
line: The palace needs someone capable. Do not take that personally.

thought: he's looking for someone who can get a job done, still
line: I am looking for someone who can get a job done. I shall keep looking.

thought: prince missing, and they admire the architecture
line: Our prince is missing, and you are admiring the architecture?

thought: something tells him they'd ask about payment first
line: Something tells me you would ask about payment first.

thought: with the prince gone every offer counts, even theirs
line: With the prince gone we must hear every offer. Even, it seems, yours.

thought: no climbing while the palace is in mourning, well, worry
line: Kindly do not climb the palace while we are in mourning. Well, worry.

thought: aside: the prince taken and adventurers come to gawp
line: The prince is taken, and the adventurers come to gawp at the windows.

thought: he can usually tell whether someone is capable
line: Are you capable? Do not answer, one can usually tell.

thought: the reward is ready and he's counted it twice
line: The reward is counted and waiting. I counted it twice.

thought: Osman says a plan is in hand and nothing more
line: Osman tells me a plan is in hand. Osman tells me very little else.

thought: he's told the Emir there is hope; hopes it's true
line: I have told the Emir there is hope. I do hope I have not lied.

thought: the Emir asks after his son constantly
line: Every hour the prince is away, the Emir asks again.

thought: the prince's rooms are kept ready, optimism or habit
line: The prince's rooms are aired and ready. Optimism, or habit.

thought: the city can afford the reward but not the loss
line: We can afford the reward. We cannot afford to lose the prince.

thought: someone is finally acting; maybe he'll sleep
line: Someone is finally doing something. I may even sleep tonight.

thought: Osman's secrecy reaches even the Chancellor
line: Not even the Chancellor may know the plan, says Osman. My own palace!

thought: they're helping Osman; the palace is grateful already
line: You are the one helping Osman. The palace is in your debt already.

thought: thanks for taking it on; the Emir will hear
line: Thank you for taking this on. The Emir will hear of it.

thought: Osman trusts slowly; if he trusts them, so does Hassan
line: Osman does not trust easily. If he trusts you, so do I.

thought: the reward waits on the prince's return; confidence in them
line: Your reward is ready whenever the prince is. I have every confidence.

thought: it does an old official good to see real effort
line: It does an old chancellor good to see someone actually trying.

thought: aside to the court: there goes the one who answered for the prince
line: There goes the one who answered for the prince. Every courtesy, now.

thought: he takes some credit for spotting them
line: I knew you were the capable sort. I said as much to Osman, roughly.

thought: water for life if they bring him home
line: Bring him home and you shall never pay for water in this city again.

thought: polite reminder that the prince isn't home
line: The prince is still not home. I mention it only in passing.

thought: politeness as a weapon: don't let him keep them
line: Do not let me keep you. Truly. The prince is waiting.

thought: the reward is for bringing him back, not for visits
line: You are aware the reward is for bringing him back, not visiting me?

thought: Osman vouches for them; Osman has been wrong before
line: Osman assures me you are capable. Osman has been wrong before.

thought: they're strolling; he hopes the prince enjoys the wait
line: Strolling, I see. I do hope the prince is enjoying his wait.

thought: what to tell the Emir: that they were browsing?
line: The Emir asks after his son daily. Shall I tell him you were browsing?

thought: it's a reward, not a pension
line: We are paying a reward for this, you understand. Not a pension.

thought: he'd offer water but they'd stop to drink it
line: I would offer you water, but I fear you would stop to drink it.

thought: his robes and papyrus are what the desert lacks
line: Robes and papyrus! The desert never has enough of either.

thought: one man, one stall, a whole city to sell to
line: Two hands for the whole of Al Kharid. I need more hands.

thought: the gnomes scoff at his carpets
line: The gnomes say my carpets will never take off. My carpets disagree.

thought: proud of his son at the Grand Exchange
line: My boy Farid sells at the Grand Exchange now. Takes after his father.

thought: sell a carpet and lose his monopoly? never
line: Sell a carpet? And have every rug merchant fly for himself? Never.

thought: Pollnivneach his start, Al Kharid his customers
line: Pollnivneach gave me my start. Al Kharid gives me my customers.

thought: business is always good, with him
line: Business is good, my friend. With me, business is always good.

thought: he never buys, as a matter of principle
line: I never buy, my friend. Buying is how a merchant becomes poor.

thought: a passer-by with apparent taste
line: My friend, you have the look of someone with excellent taste.

thought: a discerning customer, he can always tell
line: Ah, a customer of discernment! One sees so few.

thought: a fine traveller deserves a fine robe, which he sells
line: Such a fine traveller deserves a fine robe, and I happen to sell them.

thought: a special price, said to almost nobody
line: For you, my friend, a special price. I say that to almost nobody.

thought: a sharp eye that could almost sell like him
line: With an eye like yours you could sell. Nearly as well as me, even.

thought: they look like a person of means
line: I can see you are a person of means, my friend. Means and taste.

thought: he never forgets a good customer, and has decided this is one
line: I never forget a good customer, my friend. I shall not forget you.

thought: aside to the camel by his stall: there walks a customer with taste
line: Now there walks a customer with taste. Mark my words.

thought: browsing never made anyone rich
line: Browsing again? Browsing never made anyone rich, my friend.

thought: a heavy purse that never opens at his stall
line: Such a heavy purse, my friend, and it never once opens at my stall.

thought: they'd make a terrible merchant, walking past bargains
line: You would make a terrible merchant. You walk past every bargain.

thought: he could sell them a bucket they don't need, two even
line: I could sell you a bucket you do not need. I could sell you two.

thought: every adventurer needs a tinderbox, surely
line: An adventurer with nothing to buy? Every adventurer needs a tinderbox.

thought: a raw chicken would improve their day
line: Forgive me, my friend, but a raw chicken would improve your day.

thought: ignoring him like a gnome would
line: Ignoring me like a gnome, my friend? Very well. I can wait.

thought: haggling by walking away; he invented that
line: Haggling by walking away, my friend? I invented that trick.

thought: the nephew should be here by now
line: My nephew should be here by now. Pollnivneach is not so very far.

thought: still no nephew; the stall opens at dawn
line: Still no nephew. And the stall opens at dawn, every dawn.

thought: a month's wages to fetch him; the cost stings
line: A month of the boy's wages, just to fetch him. A month!

thought: with the boy here he could sell twice as much
line: If the boy were here, I could sell twice as much. Twice!

thought: family is family but punctual family is better
line: Family is family, my friend, but punctual family is better.

thought: who minds the stall while he sells?
line: Who minds the stall while I sell? Not my nephew, apparently.

thought: a nephew-shaped gap behind the counter
line: There is a nephew-shaped gap behind my counter, my friend.

thought: no dragons for a shopkeeper, only a missing nephew
line: No dragons to slay at a stall. Only a nephew to wait for.

thought: good feet for a long road south
line: Good strong feet, my friend. Feet that could reach Pollnivneach.

thought: they look trustworthy, and he has a nephew problem
line: You look trustworthy, my friend, and I have a nephew problem.

thought: a capable face; he could use one
line: Ah, a capable face! I could use a capable face, my friend.

thought: they'd make a better assistant than the one who never came
line: You would make a fine assistant. Better than the one who never came.

thought: they're clearly the reliable sort; rarer than an honest camel
line: Such a reliable look about you, my friend. Rarer than an honest camel.

thought: for a friend, robes nearly half price
line: For a friend like you, the robes are nearly half price. Nearly.

thought: aside to a camel: there goes someone who'd get to Pollnivneach and back
line: Now there goes someone who would get to Pollnivneach and back.

thought: someone who turns up when expected, unlike his nephew
line: A traveller who arrives when expected! A rare jewel, my friend.

thought: too busy to buy, too busy to help
line: Too busy to buy and too busy to help. What are you for, my friend?

thought: nephew lost somewhere, customer lost at his stall
line: My nephew is lost somewhere, and you are lost in front of my stall.

thought: he'd hire them, but would have to watch them
line: I would hire you myself, my friend, but I would have to watch you.

thought: they dawdle almost as well as the nephew
line: You dawdle, my friend, almost as well as my nephew does.

thought: not buying? stand aside for the customers
line: Not buying? Then at least stand aside for the customers.

thought: everyone wants a bargain, nobody wants a job
line: Everyone wants a bargain and nobody wants a job. Is that not so?

thought: not 'no', just 'later'
line: Not interested? I shall put you down as 'later', my friend.

thought: empty hands he could fill for a fair price
line: Such empty hands. I could fill them for a very fair price.

thought: sold a beard and headdress early; good day
line: A beard and a headdress, sold before breakfast. A good day.

thought: any word from the south? no
line: Any word from Pollnivneach? No? Then the boy is still out there.

thought: he keeps spare false beards; one never knows
line: I keep a spare false beard for emergencies. One never knows.

thought: someone is fetching the boy; coins are coming
line: Someone is finally fetching the boy. I can almost hear the coins.

thought: the nephew will be greeted by a stranger in a fake beard
line: My nephew will be so pleased to meet a stranger in a false beard.

thought: when the boy arrives he'll rest; no, he'll sell more
line: When the boy arrives I shall take a day off... no, I shall sell more.

thought: a month's wages for one nephew: expensive family
line: A month of wages for one nephew. Expensive family, mine.

thought: the beard was a bargain; could have charged double
line: That beard was a bargain. I could have charged double, and did not.

thought: the beard he sold them suited them
line: That beard suited you, my friend. Very convincing.

thought: off to fetch his nephew: a true friend of the family
line: Off to Pollnivneach for me? A true friend of the family!

thought: only they would go; he'll remember, at a discount
line: Only you would go. I shall remember that, my friend, at a discount.

thought: such dedication they might make a salesman
line: Such dedication! You would make a salesman yet, my friend.

thought: first look at new stock when the boy is back
line: When the boy is back, you shall have the first look at my new stock.

thought: with them on it the nephew is as good as home
line: A traveller of your talents, finding my nephew? He is as good as home.

thought: they bargain badly but travel well
line: You bargain badly but you travel well. I respect the second.

thought: in his headdress they'll pass for a local, nearly
line: With my headdress on, they will take you for a local. Nearly.

thought: still here? the road runs south
line: Still here? Pollnivneach is south, my friend. Very south.

thought: nephew out there, adventurer in here looking at buckets
line: My nephew is out there, and you are in here, looking at buckets.

thought: did the beard fall off? no refunds
line: Did the beard fall off already? I do not do refunds.

thought: another disguise will cost more now
line: If you need another disguise, I am afraid the price has gone up.

thought: slower and more stubborn than a camel
line: Slower than a camel with a grudge, my friend, and twice as stubborn.

thought: promised a nephew, not a sightseer
line: I was promised a nephew, my friend, not a sightseer.

thought: the boy will have a real beard by the time they get there
line: The boy will have grown a real beard by the time you get there.

thought: lost the way? buy papyrus and draw a map
line: Lost the way? Buy some papyrus from me and draw yourself a map.

thought: the gate needs mending; sand in the hinges
line: The gate needs mending again. Sand gets into everything, even hinges.

thought: a small toll and still they look at him like a bandit
line: A small toll, and still they look at me as if I were a bandit.

thought: a dry traveller came back through, waterskin empty
line: Another empty waterskin back through the gate, and a very dry owner.

thought: the cell is empty; suspicious
line: The cell is empty today. I always find that suspicious.

thought: his guards call his prices reasonable; he pays them
line: My guards say my price is very reasonable. I do pay their wages.

thought: the chest: his men carry it to the bank
line: Things left in the chest go to the bank. My men carry them. Simple.

thought: other passes down at Unkah
line: There are passes down at Unkah too. Same sand, different gate.

thought: someone he jailed walks free again; Port Sarim, he supposes
line: Someone I jailed is walking about free again. Port Sarim, I suppose.

thought: he wagers they actually read the billboard
line: Ah, effendi! I would wager you actually read the billboard.

thought: a traveller who pays the toll without complaint
line: A traveller who pays the toll without complaint! My favourite kind.

thought: he reckons the sands will give this one back
line: Something tells me the sands will give you back, effendi.

thought: a familiar face; they keep the peace, he keeps the gate
line: Hello again, friend. You keep the peace, and I keep the gate.

thought: sensible people pack a knife and water; they look sensible
line: Sensible folk bring a knife and a full waterskin. You look sensible.

thought: they don't walk like an outlaw; outlaws slink
line: No outlaw walks the way you do, friend. Outlaws slink.

thought: he'd trust them with the bank chest, and he trusts nobody
line: I would trust you with the bank chest, effendi, and I trust nobody.

thought: aside to his guard: the sands won't get that one
line: There goes someone the sands will not get. Mark it.

thought: thinking of declaring themselves an outlaw? the cell has room
line: Thinking of calling yourself an outlaw? The cell has room.

thought: they'll come back thirsty and blame him
line: You will come back thirsty, effendi, and you will blame me.

thought: cacti have more sense, and they stand still
line: I have seen cacti with more sense, effendi, and they stand still.

thought: did they read the billboard? of course not
line: Did you read the billboard? No, of course not.

thought: haggling over a small toll wounds him
line: Haggling over a small toll? With me? I am wounded, effendi.

thought: misattribution: did he lock them up once?
line: Did I not lock you up once? No? My mistake, effendi.

thought: the sands have swallowed people with more sense
line: The sands have swallowed travellers with far more sense than you.

thought: a fond farewell with a cell kept warm
line: So long, effendi. I shall keep a cell warm for you.

thought: Irena watches the gate all day
line: Poor Irena. She watches the gate from dawn to dusk.

thought: the girl went south and the gate hasn't seen her since
line: That girl went south, and my gate has not seen her since.

thought: Irena asks every morning and he has nothing to tell
line: Irena asks me every morning. Every morning I have nothing to tell her.

thought: days now; the desert doesn't give people back easily
line: Days, now. The desert does not give people back after days.

thought: he wishes he'd checked her waterskin
line: I should have looked at her waterskin more closely. I should have.

thought: his men watch for the girl and see only sand
line: My men keep watch for the girl. They see only sand.

thought: worse than any sandstorm: a mother crying at the gate
line: Worse than any sandstorm, a mother crying by the gate.

thought: could outlaws be to blame? he hopes not
line: No word of Irena's girl. Outlaws would not dare... would they?

thought: a capable traveller; Irena would be glad of them
line: A capable traveller, effendi. Irena would be glad to meet you.

thought: they go into the sands prepared
line: You go into the sands prepared, friend. Not everyone does.

thought: kind eyes; Irena could use those now
line: You have kind eyes. Irena could do with kind eyes just now.

thought: a steady face after a sorrowful week
line: Good to see a steady face. This gate has seen enough sorrow lately.

thought: some walk out of the desert again; they look like one
line: Some people walk out of the desert again, effendi. You look like one.

thought: a traveller who stops to listen
line: A traveller who stops to listen. Irena has had too few of those.

thought: they pay the toll and heed the billboard
line: You pay your toll and you mind the billboard. Rare virtues, effendi.

thought: aside to a guard: there's someone a mother could trust
line: There goes someone a mother could trust. Not many come through here.

thought: don't get lost as well; one is enough
line: Mind you do not get lost as well, effendi. One is enough.

thought: did they read the billboard or just look at it?
line: Did you read the billboard, effendi, or just admire the lettering?

thought: another self-declared outlaw joker
line: Outlaw, are you? Every joker says so. The cell has heard it all.

thought: heroes come through daily; the desert keeps some
line: Heroes come through here every day. The desert keeps quite a few.

thought: aside: that one never glanced at the billboard
line: That one never even glanced at the billboard. Mark my words.

thought: he'd rather sell them a robe than a pass
line: I would sell you a pass, effendi, but I would rather sell you a robe.

thought: the sort to go in without a waterskin
line: You look the sort to go in without a waterskin. Prove me wrong.

thought: Irena needs a hero; let's hope one comes along
line: Irena needs a hero. Let us both hope one comes along soon.

thought: Irena smiled today; someone is looking
line: Irena smiled today, for the first time in days. Someone is looking.

thought: brave, going after the girl; foolish maybe
line: Brave, going after the girl. Foolish, maybe, but brave.

thought: he keeps a waterskin by the gate for Ana's return
line: I keep a full waterskin by the gate for Ana, for when she comes back.

thought: he asks every traveller from the south
line: Every traveller from the south, I ask about the girl. Nothing yet.

thought: Irena has stopped crying and watches the dunes
line: Irena has stopped crying. Now she just watches the dunes.

thought: his men watch for two now: the girl and her finder
line: My men watch for two people now. The girl, and whoever finds her.

thought: hope is no trade; he only sells waterskins
line: Hope is a hard thing to sell. Luckily, I only sell waterskins.

thought: a wide desert, a small girl, but someone looking
line: The desert is wide and one girl is small. Still, someone is looking.

thought: recognises them as the one searching for Ana
line: You are the one looking for Ana? Brave, effendi. Truly brave.

thought: Irena talks of nobody else now
line: Irena talks of nobody but you now, friend.

thought: an extra waterskin for the searcher, on the house
line: Take an extra waterskin, friend. On the house, this once.

thought: going after another's child; he respects it
line: A brave thing, going after another's child. I respect it.

thought: if anyone can bring her home, he'd bet on them
line: If anyone can bring that girl home, effendi, I would bet on you.

thought: they gave a mother hope
line: You gave a mother hope. That is worth more than any pass I sell.

thought: the desert doesn't frighten them; it frightens him
line: The desert does not frighten you. Good. It frightens me.

thought: his men won't keep the searcher waiting
line: My men will not keep you waiting at the gate, friend. Not today.

thought: back already, without the girl?
line: Back already, and without the girl? The desert is that way, effendi.

thought: Irena's hopes rest on them; walk faster
line: Irena's hopes rest on you. I would walk a little faster.

thought: brave yes, prepared we'll see
line: Brave, yes. Prepared? We shall see, effendi.

thought: if they need rescuing too, he's not going in
line: If you need rescuing as well, I am not going in after you.

thought: hope they search better than they shop
line: I do hope you search better than you shop, friend.

thought: don't come back without her; well, do come back
line: Do not come back without her. Well, do come back, but with her.

thought: try not to be the next one Irena waits for
line: So long, effendi. Try not to be the next one Irena waits for.

thought: aside: a rescuer standing about at the gate
line: A rescuer standing about at my gate. Irena would be thrilled.

thought: his feet ache; he still thinks about the Christmas the Duke gave him a chair
line: The Duke gave me a chair once, you know. From his own room.

thought: another treasure hunter has just been sent to him with a scroll
line: Treasure hunters again. Why does every scroll send them to me?

thought: someone raised their voice in the courtyard and it brought back the stranger who threatened them all
line: Still can't hear a raised voice without thinking of that awful man.

thought: rehearsing the directions he gives every lost newcomer
line: North over the river for Varrock, upstairs for the Duke.

thought: keeping his direction on the round
line: Clockwise, always clockwise. The other way would feel all wrong.

thought: word came that someone has mastered every skill; he sends his congratulations by magic
line: Another one's mastered every skill. I'll send my congratulations.

thought: caught pausing, he has an excuse ready
line: If anyone asks, I'm not resting. I'm inspecting the flagstones.

thought: the day's fresh arrivals, eager as they always are
line: New faces in the courtyard again. They all look so keen.

thought: he remembers how long this one has been about, and it suits them
line: You've been about a good while now. It shows, in a nice way.

thought: they don't stop to ask the way; he checks himself and is pleased
line: Not lost, are you? No, you know your way now.

thought: an armed stranger passed and he didn't startle
line: You didn't make me jump at all. Most strangers make me jump.

thought: he remembers every face, and this one fondly
line: I never forget a face, and yours I'm always glad of.

thought: points them out to someone: he saw them arrive, green
line: Look at that one. Came through here green as grass, once.

thought: they walk like someone with business elsewhere now
line: Off somewhere grand, I expect. You've that walk about you now.

thought: most people want directions or a clue casket from him; this one wants nothing
line: A face that wants neither directions nor a casket. How refreshing.

thought: as the Duke's servant he'd put in a word for a polite one
line: If the Duke ever asks who's polite round here, I'll say you.

thought: assumes they're lost again and gives the same directions, pointedly
line: Lost again? Varrock's north over the river, same as last time.

thought: they came in briskly and frightened him; it reminded him of the man who threatened everyone
line: Must you stride in like that? I thought it was that man again.

thought: they're crossing his round the wrong way
line: Clockwise, if you please. You're walking against the flow.

thought: he remembers them arriving eager; the eagerness seems to have gone
line: You arrived looking so eager. Whatever happened to that?

thought: grumbles to someone nearby that this one never greets him
line: That one's never once stopped to say hello. Not once.

thought: adventurers rush through his courtyard without a wave
line: Adventurers. Always in a rush, and not one of them waves.

thought: he hands caskets to treasure hunters; this one just looks the grasping type
line: No casket for you. You just look like someone who'd want one.

thought: he's watched countless newcomers; this one is merely one of them
line: Seen ever so many come through, and you're... well, one of them.

thought: his back still hurts from the day clearing the cellar
line: All day clearing that cellar. My back's still complaining.

thought: he didn't feel any earthquake but won't doubt the Duke
line: An earthquake, the Duke says. I never felt it, but he'd know.

thought: rubble isn't a servant's job
line: Rubble, rubble, rubble... I'm a servant, not a mole.

thought: the cellar frightens him now
line: Nobody's getting me back in that cellar. Not after the wall went.

thought: he has his escape planned for the next tremor
line: If the ground shakes again, I'll be first under the table.

thought: the Cook has been grumbling about dust in the ingredients
line: Cook's still finding cellar dust in his flour. He's not pleased.

thought: the Duke is waiting on builders and Hans is watching for them
line: Still no builders for that cellar wall. I keep watching the bridge.

thought: only one wall came down; he counts it a mercy
line: Funny sort of earthquake, just the one wall. Lucky, really.

thought: this one looks steady; he'd want them about in a tremor
line: You've a steady look. I'd want you about if the ground shook again.

thought: they're heading indoors near the cellar, which he won't go near
line: Going near that cellar? You're braver than I am.

thought: he swept all day and they haven't tracked anything in
line: Thank you for not treading rubble about. I swept all day.

thought: a calm face after weeks of nerves
line: A calm face, at last. I've been all nerves since the wall fell in.

thought: this one wouldn't panic the way he does
line: That one'd not run screaming from an earthquake. Not like some.

thought: an adventurer would have cleared the rubble much faster than him
line: You'd have cleared that cellar in half the time, I expect.

thought: the Duke is waiting on builders; he'd put this one forward
line: If the Duke wants strong arms for that wall, I'll mention you.

thought: walls coming down and this one is perfectly cheerful
line: Walls falling in, and you strolling about cheerful as anything.

thought: misattribution: perhaps this clumsy adventurer knocked the wall in
line: Not you who knocked the cellar wall in, is it? You've the elbows.

thought: they have time for adventures but nobody helped him sweep
line: Plenty of time for adventures, I see. None for sweeping.

thought: their footsteps made him think the cellar was going again
line: Heavy-footed, aren't you? I thought the cellar was going again.

thought: stomping adventurers and falling walls, in his mind connected
line: Adventurers. Stomp about all day, and then walls fall in.

thought: offers them the rubble job, knowing the answer
line: Want a job? There's rubble, if you're not too grand for it.

thought: loyal to the Duke's account, suspects the stranger of spreading talk

thought: peace is made but they still march about like a soldier

thought: not everyone liked the treaty, and some blame them

thought: this peacemaker still asks him the way

thought: with Sigmund dismissed, his errands fell to Hans

thought: he'd thank them but they never stop moving, which is rich from him

thought: worries the goblins will pick up adventurer habits

thought: nobody asked him about the new neighbours, though he likes them

thought: remembers the lookouts his father posted against Elvarg

thought: Crandor was grand in his father's day, then went silent

thought: signing trading permits; prosperity means paperwork
line: Another permit to sign. Prosperity is a great deal of paperwork.

thought: watches Hans going round and approves

thought: he keeps a careful eye on his limited shields

thought: the Cook boasts of the new range; the Duke has yet to see results

thought: someone asked about staff holidays; out of the question

thought: this one looks useful to a duke
line: You have the look of someone who gets things done, adventurer.

thought: brave without being reckless, the quality he values

thought: the sort of character Lumbridge wants

thought: tells his servant this one has manners

thought: his father would have made this one a lookout

thought: notices a traveller with purpose

thought: rank-minded: the peasantry could learn from this one

thought: courage noted; restraint lacking

thought: tells Hans to watch this one near the silver
line: Hans, do keep an eye on that one near the silver.

thought: he's heard adventurers are useful; still waiting

thought: he stands only for the worthy

thought: he'd send them on an errand but values the errand

line: Do adventurers ever knock, or is that a knightly habit?

thought: Sedridor should have it, but he can't leave

thought: heard the wizards are hunting artefacts

thought: the tower isn't far, for anyone free to go

thought: he doesn't know what to do with it, so he polished it

thought: if this was in the cellar junk, what else is?

thought: it wants a proper adventurer, not any passing peasant

thought: judging its age, or its dirt

thought: trustworthiness matters with a precious object

thought: envies their freedom to travel

thought: trust measured in distance to the tower

thought: they have a learned air; perhaps they know talismans

thought: sensible and on foot, the kind the wizards would want

thought: they could carry something curious safely

thought: doubts they'd get it past the bridge

thought: wonders if the wizards would even admit them

thought: keep this one out of the cellar; enough has turned up there

thought: fears they'd sell it

thought: Sedridor wants clever people; implies this one isn't

thought: marvels that a cellar trinket led to a hidden mine

thought: he always knew it mattered, he tells himself

thought: the shelf where the talisman sat is empty now

thought: wonders about recognition

thought: repeats what the wizards call it, without quite understanding

thought: providence working through his cellar

thought: tempted to search the cellar again

thought: the wizards got a mine and he got nothing

thought: recognises the one who carried his talisman

thought: they did Lumbridge credit

thought: tells Hans to bow to the finder of the mine

thought: he picked well, and says so

thought: would trust them with all his letters now

thought: the next cellar mystery is theirs

thought: Saradomin favoured the errand and the runner

thought: his talisman, their feet: a partnership

thought: one walk and they think themselves important

thought: reminds them he found the talisman; they only walked

thought: warns Hans to hide anything else from the cellar

thought: a single delivery doesn't make a wizard

thought: credit is due, mostly to him

thought: the goat needs feeding and the children won't

thought: wonders what the Duke's table is like with unburnt food

thought: they look kitchen-capable

thought: still going strong, unlike him

thought: a helpful sort; he might ask after all

thought: the goat dislikes everyone but would like this one

thought: an offer of food, not cake

thought: steady hands, never dropped an egg

thought: someone like this could save a birthday

thought: sulky: don't mind him losing his job

thought: they'd step over an egg

thought: keeps spare flour now

thought: plans to buy ingredients ahead next time

thought: the Duke prefers edible food to their cooking

thought: they're back for another job; there are no more birthdays

thought: he avoids the bell ropes; Urhney still teases him about them

thought: no letter from Draynor in a while

thought: Urhney took the swamp; he got the church

thought: Saradomin made the world with his brothers, and is the tidy one

thought: he always read the god wars as a parable

thought: Saradomin's following outgrows his pews

thought: relieved this one has surely heard of Saradomin

thought: the church is open to folk like this most of all

thought: remarks to someone that here walks a decent soul

thought: they'd be a good bearer of the Wise Old Man's letters

thought: even the hermit Urhney might smile at them

thought: light against dark; they're on the side of light

thought: they passed his door without sneering

thought: they look lost; surely they've heard of Saradomin

thought: the church has been open for centuries; they might try it

thought: never seen this one in church

thought: he'll pray for them, and means it pointedly

thought: hurrying past a house of Saradomin is noticed

thought: they look like they'd get stuck up the bell ropes, as he did

thought: Zamorakians rush like that; surely not this one

thought: a short sermon would help

thought: prayers and holy water failed; now he's ignoring it

thought: he tried an exorcist's cry; it didn't work

thought: two centuries of peaceful burials, and now this

thought: of all places to haunt, a church

thought: something cold passed him in the graveyard

thought: mourners have stopped visiting the graves

thought: judges the ghost persistent rather than wicked

thought: they don't look like a ghost would frighten them; it frightens him

thought: perhaps Saradomin sent them past

thought: this one would stand in a haunted graveyard unblinking
line: There's someone who'd stand in a haunted graveyard and not blink.

thought: steady nerves; even Urhney would talk to them

thought: a calm traveller, rare since the haunting
line: Ah, a calm traveller! We've had little calm since the haunting.

thought: a good soul would ease any ghost

thought: they walk past the haunted graveyard coolly

thought: Saradomin's light in them; ghosts can't abide that, he hopes

thought: if they dawdle the ghost will think they're staying

thought: adventurers fight dragons but find themselves busy for a ghost

thought: they might look holier with a ghost watching

thought: a fine adventurer, with a ghost still loose

thought: Saradomin sees who walks past a haunting

thought: off to save the world; the graveyard can wait

thought: gently teases them for being ghost-shy

thought: surely not scared of one small ghost

thought: a warlock stealing skulls; nothing is safe

thought: hopes Urhney was polite to the helper; he rarely is

thought: he hears it moaning, but now there's hope

thought: why would a warlock want a ghost's skull?

thought: lit candles for the ghost and the helper

thought: things are moving, slowly

thought: no sleep, but it's being seen to

thought: he stopped saying good night to the graveyard because it answers

thought: blesses them for taking the ghost on

thought: getting kindness out of Urhney is a feat

thought: points out the one seeing to the ghost

thought: chasing a skull a warlock stole is braver than he'd be

thought: sleeps easier knowing they're on it

thought: they're in and out of the graveyard like a regular

thought: most would have given up by now

thought: Saradomin chose well sending them

thought: they're slow; the ghost literally isn't going anywhere

thought: notes it's still haunted, without hurrying anyone

thought: Urhney probably grumbled at them; he spots idlers

thought: this one is meant to be laying the ghost, unhurried
line: That one's meant to be laying our ghost. In no hurry, it seems.

thought: if a warlock found a skull, an adventurer can

thought: he prayed for help and got this one; a test
line: I prayed for help, and Saradomin sent you. He does test us.

thought: he'd like to bury people in peace
line: Some of us would like to bury people in peace, traveller.
