thought: the ball won't say more
line: Something gathers in the south. The ball won't say more, the tease.

thought: looks like a rune buyer
line: You look like someone who'd appreciate a good rune. Or several?

thought: a friendly face; offers tea
line: A friendly face! Do stop for tea, if you've the time.

thought: a magical look; runes would suit
line: You've a magical sort of look about you. Runes would suit you.

thought: an eye for runes Sedridor would like
line: An eye for runes, I can tell. Sedridor would approve of you.

thought: trustworthy, nearly, with the costly runes
line: An honest face. I'd trust you with my death runes. Nearly.

thought: might master runecraft and buy the cape
line: I'll sell you the cape one day, I shouldn't wonder.

thought: careful people make good runecrafters
line: Careful sort, are you? Good. Runecraft rewards the careful.

thought: a sensible customer, easy to spot
line: Now that's a customer with a bit of sense. One can always tell.

thought: just browsing; he minds a bit
line: Just looking, are we? The runes don't mind. I mind a little.

thought: they ignored the death runes
line: Honestly. Straight past the death runes. Nobody does that.

thought: mind runes for the mind, pointedly
line: Mind runes for you, I'd guess. For, ah... the mind.

thought: Sedridor would judge them as he judges Aubury
line: Sedridor would say you're not much of a wizard. He says it of me, too.

thought: they don't know what a rune is; politely fine
line: Do you know what a rune is? No, no, it's fine. Most don't.

thought: adventurers buy one rune and dream big
line: Adventurers buy one fire rune and want to set the world alight.

thought: would offer tea but fears spills
line: I'd offer you tea, but you look like you'd spill it on the stock.

thought: runecraft is still lost on some
line: Runecraft was a lost art for an age. For some it still is.

thought: the rarer runes running low
line: Chaos runes running low again. Death runes too, if I'm honest.

thought: muddled over a book swap with Reldo
line: Reldo still has my book on... no, I have his. One of us has it.

thought: the kettle's on for anyone
line: Kettle's on, if anyone wants tea. Anyone at all.

thought: agrees with Sedridor's verdict on him
line: Sedridor says I'm not much of a wizard. Quite right. I'm a rune man.

thought: amazed runecraft was ever lost
line: Runecrafting was lost once, you know. Lost! Can you imagine?

thought: nobody wonders how runes are made
line: Lovely things, runes. Nobody ever stops to wonder how they're made.

thought: pleased with his shop's spot by the bank
line: A rune shop wants a bank close by. I chose my spot well.

thought: body runes don't sell
line: Body runes. Little treasures. Hardly anyone buys them.

thought: curious look; turns up interesting things
line: You've a curious look. The sort who turns up interesting things.

thought: an adventurer stopping at a rune shop
line: An adventurer who stops at a rune shop! There's hope for you yet.

thought: they'd get on with Sedridor
line: You'd get on with Sedridor, I think. He likes a bright face.

thought: clever-looking; points them to the chaos runes
line: A clever-looking sort. The chaos runes are just there, if you like.

thought: they have patience for runecraft
line: If you ever take an interest in runecraft, you've the patience for it.

thought: a reader; Reldo would like them
line: You look like a reader. Reldo would like you, and so do I.

thought: a proper customer by their stance
line: Ah, a proper customer. One can tell from the way they stand.

thought: a new face; tea is fresh
line: Lovely to see a new face. The tea's fresh, if you've a moment.

thought: people think runes grow on trees
line: Runes don't grow on trees, you know. I'm asked weekly.

thought: they'd waste a death rune
line: You look like you'd use a death rune to light a fire. Please don't.

thought: browsing and breathing on the stock
line: Browsing again? The runes are for buying, not for breathing on.

thought: neither is much of a wizard; keep it quiet
line: Not much of a wizard, are you? Nor am I. Let's not tell Sedridor.

thought: never wondered where runes come from
line: You've never once wondered where a rune comes from, have you?

thought: here only for the tea
line: If you're only here for the tea, I'll need a word with you.

thought: spots a non-buyer by their walk
line: A customer who won't be buying, I can tell. It's in the walk.

thought: elbows near fire runes
line: Fire runes and elbows don't mix. Somebody always learns that here.

thought: wonders what Sedridor is working on
line: Sedridor's on to something new at the tower, I'd wager. He always is.

thought: a quiet day in the shop
line: Quiet day. Even the air runes look bored.

thought: Reldo's book on runecraft was thin; little is known
line: Reldo's last book on runecraft was a slim one. Not much is known.

thought: runecraft began a whole new age
line: Runecraft started a whole new age. Not bad for a little stone.

thought: chaos runes sell fast
line: Chaos runes in, chaos runes out. They never stay on the shelf long.

thought: longs for something new to study
line: I'd dearly love something new to study. Runes are lovely, but quiet.

thought: customers leave before tea
line: Tea for one again. Customers do rush off.

thought: selling is a living, making is an art
line: Selling runes is a living. Making them, now... that's an art.

thought: grateful for their help with the research
line: You've been a great help with the research, adventurer. Truly.

thought: trusts them with coded notes
line: You've a head for secrets. I'd trust you with my coded notes.

thought: they'd share credit if the incantation returns
line: If the incantation comes back, it'll be partly your doing.

thought: they don't leap to conclusions either
line: You don't leap to conclusions, I see. My sort of person.

thought: they've earned tea
line: Tea, adventurer? You've earned it, running about for us rune folk.

thought: the old tower's secrets in safe hands
line: The old tower's secrets in safe hands at last. Yours, I mean.

thought: the research's best helper goes by
line: There goes the best help this research has had in years.

thought: back again; hopes for news but won't keep them
line: Ah, back again! Any news? No, no, don't let me keep you.

thought: warns them off his notes
line: You'll not peek at my notes, will you? They're in code anyway.

thought: research moves at an adventurer's pace
line: Research crawls along at an adventurer's pace, which is slowly.

thought: don't drop things on the way to the tower
line: Do try not to drop anything on the way to the tower. Honestly.

thought: they can't read code, which is the point
line: Can you read code? No? Good, that's rather the point.

thought: slow enough for the tower to rebuild
line: Any slower, and the old tower would have rebuilt itself.

thought: running errands but never buying
line: Courier and customer both, and you still haven't bought a rune.

thought: they've jumped to conclusions
line: Conclusions are for later. You, I see, have jumped to several.

thought: errands for wizards; sweeping next
line: Errands for wizards! That one will be sweeping the tower next.

thought: everything in code, with copies
line: Every page in code, and a copy of every page. Thorough, that's me.

thought: excited, then reins himself in
line: If Sedridor's discovery fits my notes... no, no. Too soon to say.

thought: hopes to recover what the fire took
line: So much was lost when the old tower burned. We may get some back.

thought: lost his duplicate notes
line: Where did I put the duplicates? Code is no use if one can't find it.

thought: steadying himself, no leaps
line: No jumping to conclusions, Aubury. Steady, now.

thought: research over shopkeeping today
line: The shop can mind itself today. I've research on.

thought: tea gone cold over research
line: Tea's gone cold again. Research does that.

thought: the wrong sort can't read his notes
line: If the wrong sort read my notes... well, they won't. Code, you see.

thought: they look like they'd feed a cat
line: You've a cat-feeding sort of face, dear. I can always tell.

thought: helpful-looking, unlike her boys
line: Well well! A helpful-looking sort. Not like my boys, bless them.

thought: kind hands animals would trust
line: You've kind hands, dear. Animals know these things, and so do I.

thought: no sewer smell on them
line: Not a whiff of sewer on you, dear. You'd be amazed how rare that is.

thought: they'd be good with a kitten
line: You'd do well with a kitten, I think. Patient. Gentle.

thought: would stop for a stray cat, not a dog
line: A good sort, you. The sort who'd stop for a stray. Not a dog, mind.

thought: Bob would like this one
line: Bob would take to that one, I'll bet. He's a fine judge, that cat.

thought: raised right
line: Oh, you've that look, dear. Like somebody raised you right.

thought: smells of the sewers
line: Been in the sewers? You have, haven't you? I can tell, dear.

thought: looks like the hungry strays
line: You've a look of those stray dogs at the west gate. Hungry, I mean.

thought: her boys have no manners, and still beat them
line: My boys have better manners, and my boys have none.

thought: wouldn't trust them with a kitten
line: I'd not trust you with a kitten. A goldfish, perhaps. Just about.

thought: wipe your feet; enough mud already
line: Wipe your feet, dear. I've enough mud with four boys.

thought: adventurers never help at home
line: Adventurers. Always off somewhere, never a hand with the washing.

thought: they'd forget to feed a cat and blame it
line: You look like you'd forget to feed a cat, then blame the cat.

thought: grubbier than her sewer-loving son
line: Crumbs, that one's grubbier than Wilough, and he lives in a sewer.

thought: the boys in the sewer again
line: Shilop! Wilough! Out of that sewer this instant! Oh, crumbs.

thought: Walter away trading, oblivious
line: Walter's away trading again. He'll come home with presents, no idea.

thought: another stray kitten on the step
line: Another stray kitten on the step. Well, I can't leave it there, can I?

thought: Bob was a basket kitten once
line: Bob was a kitten in a basket once. Look at him now, the great lump.

thought: stray dogs begging at the west gate
line: Those strays at the west gate begged off me again. Flea-bitten things.

thought: her cousin's rat news
line: West Ardougne's got rats, my cousin says. I'd send her a cat, I would.

thought: fussy cats and their sardines
line: Doogle leaves on sardines. Fussy, cats are. Worse than boys.

thought: four boys and many cats
line: Four boys and a houseful of cats. Oh dear, oh dear.

thought: they look like a cat-finder
line: You look like a cat-finder, dear. Do you find cats? I think you do.

thought: Fluffs would have liked them
line: Oh, you've a kind face. Fluffs would have liked you.

thought: firm enough for her boys
line: You'd be good with my boys, I think. Firm. They need firm.

thought: spots a helpful sort, usually
line: Helpful sort, aren't you? I can always spot one. Usually.

thought: a sensible one, rare round here
line: Now there's a sensible one. Not many of those round here.

thought: they look capable; she's lost something furry
line: Crumbs, you look capable. I've lost something, you know. Furry.

thought: gentle hands a scared cat would trust
line: Gentle hands, I'd say. The sort a frightened cat might come to.

thought: sharp eyes; keep them open for a cat
line: Sharp eyes, dear. Keep them open for a lost cat, would you?

thought: they'd have tripped over a cat
line: You've not seen a cat, have you? No. You'd have tripped over it.

thought: her boys would fleece them
line: My boys would sell you a cat's whereabouts, and you'd pay. I can tell.

thought: they'd scare Fluffs further
line: You'd scare Fluffs further off, I expect. Cats know.

thought: adventuring while Fluffs is lost
line: Off adventuring while poor Fluffs is out there. Well, don't mind me.

thought: don't go in the sewer; they'd need fetching
line: Don't you go in that sewer looking for her. You'd only need fetching.

thought: a dog person's face
line: You've a dog person's face, dear. I can always tell.

thought: Shilop would take their money
line: Shilop wouldn't tell you a thing. He'd take your money, though.

thought: too busy for a lost cat
line: Everyone's too busy for a lost cat. That one too, by the look of it.

thought: calling for Fluffs
line: Fluffs? Fluffs! Oh, where's that cat got to?

thought: years of company, now gone
line: Nearly ten years she's purred at my side, and now not a whisker.

thought: the boys saw her last and won't say
line: Shilop and Wilough saw her last, and won't say a word. Little horrors.

thought: sardines out to tempt her home
line: Sardines out, doogle leaves and all. She'll smell them. Won't she?

thought: nobody to sit on her knitting
line: Oh dear, oh dear. Who's going to sit on my knitting now?

thought: the boys would charge her
line: If those boys know where Fluffs is, they'll want paying. By me!

thought: can't search; the boys need minding
line: I can't go looking myself. Who'd mind the boys? Nobody, that's who.

thought: looks twice at every cat
line: Every cat in Varrock gets a second look from me now. None is her.

thought: they're looking for Fluffs; bless them
line: You're looking for Fluffs? Oh, bless you, dear. Bless you.

thought: the kind soul searching for her cat
line: There's the kind soul out looking for my cat. Isn't that lovely?

thought: they paid her boys; too good
line: Paid my boys, did you? Oh, you're too good. They're terrors.

thought: if anyone can find her
line: If anyone can find her, it's you, dear. I've a feeling.

thought: they look worn out from searching
line: Crumbs, you've been everywhere for her, haven't you? Worn out, too.

thought: they actually look, unlike most
line: Bless you for trying, dear. Most people only say they'll look.

thought: a way with cats; Fluffs will come
line: You've a way with cats, I'm sure of it. She'll come to you.

thought: her boys could learn manners from them
line: My boys could learn a thing or two from you. Mostly manners.

thought: still no Fluffs; what have they done
line: Still no Fluffs? What have you been doing all day, dear?

thought: her boys fleeced them, surely
line: Did my boys fleece you? They did, didn't they? Oh, dear.

thought: standing about won't find her
line: You'll not find her standing about here, traveller.

thought: a cat, not a dragon
line: She's a cat, dear, not a dragon. She wants finding, not slaying.

thought: calling too loudly
line: Have you tried calling her? Softly, dear, not like a town crier.

thought: sewer-smelling people stay out of her kitchen
line: If you've been in that sewer, you're not coming near my kitchen.

thought: even Shilop would be quicker
line: Shilop could've found her quicker, and he can't find his own boots.

thought: Fluffs hides from stompers
line: Fluffs hides from people who stomp. Some people stomp.

thought: asks for news, gets none, kettle on
line: Any news of Fluffs? No? No. I'll put the kettle on.

thought: the boys are suspiciously quiet
line: The boys are being very quiet. Never a good sign, that.

thought: hopes the boys didn't overcharge
line: I hope those two didn't charge much. They will have. Little monkeys.

thought: window open and sardines out
line: I've left the window open for her, and the sardines out.

thought: someone's searching at last
line: Someone's out looking for Fluffs at last. Oh dear, I do hope...

thought: sardines and doogle should bring her
line: Sardines and doogle leaves. If that won't fetch her, nothing will.

thought: Shilop knows more than he says
line: Shilop says he knows nothing. Shilop always knows something.

thought: every creak might be her
line: Every creak on the step, I think it's her. It never is.

thought: recognises a shield-finder
line: Ah, one of our shield-finders! You'll always be welcome here.

thought: still can hardly believe it
line: You brought Arrav's shield home. I still can hardly believe it.

thought: the old case is full thanks to them
line: Thanks to you the old case isn't empty. My word, what a day that was.

thought: glad of the visit; the shield looks well
line: Kind of you to drop in. The shield looks well, doesn't it?

thought: cake saved for the finder
line: There's a slice of cake with your name on it, shield-finder.

thought: wrote their certificate with care
line: I wrote your half-certificate in my best hand, you know.

thought: history will remember them; he'll write the card
line: History will remember you, I'm sure. I'll write the card myself.

thought: points out one of the two finders
line: That's one of the two who brought the shield home. Marvellous!

thought: it took two of them
line: Only half a shield, though? Took two of you, didn't it?

thought: half a shield, half a name
line: You found half the shield. Shall I put half your name on the card?

thought: lingering in case of more reward
line: The reward's been paid, if that's why you're lingering.

thought: checking the shield hasn't gone again
line: Back to check on the shield? It hasn't wandered off. Not this time.

thought: they boast of finding it alone
line: Do stop telling people you found it alone. I have the paperwork.

thought: one find and now an archaeologist
line: One shield, and now you think you're an archaeologist. Pish-posh.

thought: the finder tramping mud past exhibits
line: There goes our shield-finder, tramping mud past the exhibits.

thought: one find and the rest of the museum bores them
line: Find one treasure and the rest of the museum bores them. Adventurers!

thought: proud of his novel half-certificates
line: Half-certificates! I'd never written one before. Rather proud of them.

thought: keeps stopping to look at the shield
line: The shield's home at last, and I do stop and look at it rather a lot.

thought: two halves, two finders
line: Two halves of a shield, and two finders to match. How tidy.

thought: celebrated with cake, twice
line: I baked a cake when the second half came in. Then another.

thought: heard the king was amazed to pay
line: The king paid his father's reward at last. Amazed, they say he was.

thought: years searching, then it walked in, in halves
line: Years we searched, and in the end it simply walked in. In halves.

thought: barely a scratch, bar the split
line: Back in its case, and hardly a scratch. Well, a crack down the middle.

thought: invites them to see it home
line: Arrav's shield, home where it belongs. Do go and look, it's lovely.

thought: welcomes a visitor with an eye for history
line: Welcome, welcome! Someone with an eye for history, I can tell.

thought: they look like a digger; wants to hear
line: You look like you've dug something up in your time. Do tell!

thought: a student of the past; cake for passing
line: A student of the past, are we? There's cake for those who pass.

thought: a visitor not touching the glass
line: My word, a visitor who doesn't touch the glass. Splendid.

thought: steady hands for the Digsite
line: You'd make a fine Digsite student. Steady hands, I see.

thought: a sense of history, rarer than a find
line: An adventurer with a sense of history! Rarer than a good find.

thought: they bring things back; the museum likes that
line: Someone who brings things back, I'd say. We like that here.

thought: someone reading every label
line: Now there's a visitor who reads the labels. Every one!

thought: they've touched the glass
line: Hands off the glass, please. History doesn't need your fingerprints.

thought: haven't passed their exams; the cake waits
line: Passed your exams yet? No? The cake will keep. Probably.

thought: wouldn't know a relic from a rock
line: You'd not know a relic from a rock, I suspect. Most don't, mind.

thought: Digsite mud on the museum floor
line: Wipe your feet. Half the Digsite comes in on adventurers' boots.

thought: adventurers hunting treasure among labelled exhibits
line: Adventurers, looking for treasure in a museum. It's all labelled!

thought: steers them to the grim relics
line: The macabre relics are over there, if that's more your sort of thing.

thought: they want a medallion; more rubies first
line: A medallion? For you? Bring a great many more rubies first.

thought: they'd sell a fossil to a trader
line: You look like you'd sell a fossil to the first trader who asked.

thought: cakes and exam papers on the go
line: Cake in the oven, exams on the desk... a curator's work is never done.

thought: the museum's zeal for treasure, a touch too keen
line: The museum goes to great lengths for a treasure. Great lengths!

thought: the shipwreck relics have grim inscriptions
line: Macabre inscriptions on these shipwreck relics. Lovely, though.

thought: stamping Digsite letters, ink everywhere
line: Another letter to stamp for the Digsite. Ink everywhere.

thought: thinks the Salve display undersells the warriors
line: Seven priestly warriors, and I still say the display undersells them.

thought: the medallion's steep price is for the museum
line: A great many rubies for a medallion. It's for the museum, you see.

thought: loves the Arrav display card
line: Arrav, best-known hero of his age! I never tire of that card.

thought: fingerprints on the display glass
line: Somebody's been touching the glass again. Fingerprints everywhere.

thought: a finder's look; the museum needs one
line: You've a finder's look about you. The museum could use one.

thought: an honest face, unlike the gang
line: My word, an honest face! The Phoenix Gang never had one of those.

thought: their sort might bring the shield back
line: If anyone brings back that shield, I'd wager it'll be your sort.

thought: sharp eyes, wasted on exhibits
line: Sharp eyes, I see. Wasted on my exhibits, really.

thought: come back with a find, ideally a shield
line: Do come back when you've found something. Ideally a shield.

thought: the greatest treasure is still missing
line: Ah, an adventurer! Our greatest treasure is still out there, you know.

thought: imagines them on a plaque
line: You'd look rather good on a plaque. Returned by... well, we'll see.

thought: a sense of history, rarer than a shield
line: Now that one has a sense of history. Rarer than a shield, nowadays.

thought: years of searching and this is his help
line: Years of searching, and my best help is you, reading the labels.

thought: the thieves had more ambition
line: The thieves who took our shield had more ambition than you, I'd say.

thought: looking for the shield in the one place it isn't
line: Looking for the shield in here? It's the one thing we haven't got.

thought: a shifty look; hopes they're no Phoenix
line: Not a Phoenix, I hope? You've a slightly shifty look about you.

thought: adventurers haven't brought it home
line: If adventurers were any good, that shield would be home by now.

thought: the reward isn't for pacing his galleries
line: The king's reward is for the shield, not for pacing my galleries.

thought: they're touching the empty case
line: Please don't touch the empty case. It's all we have left.

thought: they'd miss it round their neck
line: Pish-posh, you'd not find that shield if it hung round your neck.

thought: the prize exhibit's case is empty
line: Our prize exhibit, taken by the Phoenix Gang. The case is still empty.

thought: years of searching, nothing found
line: Years we've searched for that shield. Years! Not so much as a rivet.

thought: dusts the empty plinth out of habit
line: I dust the empty plinth every morning. Habit, I suppose.

thought: would bake a huge cake if it came home
line: If that shield ever comes home, I'll bake the biggest cake in Varrock.

thought: indignant at the theft
line: Thieves, in my museum, after Arrav's shield. The cheek of it!

thought: guesses it's gathering dust somewhere in town
line: Arrav's shield is somewhere in this city, I'd wager, gathering dust.

thought: the king's reward still stands; his patience barely
line: The king's reward still stands, they say. As does my patience. Just.

thought: it'd be a homecoming more than a find
line: It wouldn't be a find, really, more a homecoming. Still, what a day!

thought: recognises the shield-finder; thanks that talk down
line: Ah, the one who brought back Arrav's shield. You may bow, citizen.

thought: rare gratitude, with a royal warning
line: My thanks for the shield, adventurer. Do not let it swell your head.

thought: the reward went somewhere deserving, he supposes
line: My father's reward went to a worthy pocket. Yours, was it not?

thought: this one did what his father never could
line: You found what my father never could. He might have knighted you.

thought: points out the shield-finder to Aeonisig
line: Aeonisig, that is the shield-finder. Do try to look grateful.

thought: the one who cost him a fortune, said fondly
line: There goes the one who cost me a fortune, and I mean that kindly.

thought: spots the shield-finder at the door
line: Good heavens, the shield-finder. Do come in, and mind the carpets.

thought: the reward was older than the claimant, he guesses
line: You claimed a reward older than you are, I expect. Well done, citizen.

thought: the one who emptied his treasury is back
line: Ah, the one who emptied my treasury. Kindly touch nothing else.

thought: two people shared it; this was the lesser half
line: Two of you claimed that reward, I recall. You were the lesser half.

thought: half a shield each, a whole reward between them
line: Half a shield each, and a whole reward between them. Hardly fair.

thought: in case they've found another, there's no money
line: Found another shield, citizen? The treasury is out, so do not bother.

thought: tells Aeonisig to lock the treasury
line: Aeonisig, lock the treasury. The shield-finder is back.

thought: half a shield got from thieves; he'd rather not know how
line: Wherever you got that half a shield, citizen, I do not wish to know.

thought: puts the find down to luck
line: Must have been luck, finding that shield. It usually is.

thought: adventurers paid once now expect statues
line: One reward paid, and now they expect a statue. Adventurers.

thought: the reward finally paid; the treasury hadn't planned for it
line: At last I have paid my father's reward. I had not budgeted for it.

thought: shield back, treasury lighter
line: Arrav's shield back in the museum, and my treasury the lighter for it.

thought: the half-certificate business struck him as fussy
line: Half a certificate here, half there... the museum loves paperwork.

thought: a shield split between two gangs is so Varrock
line: A shield in two halves, held by two gangs. How very like Varrock.

thought: amazed it was ever claimed
line: Father would have been astonished to see it claimed. I certainly was.

thought: honour cost him; he wants that noted
line: Honour is an expensive business, citizen. Ask my treasury.

thought: the reward nearly outlived him too
line: That reward outlived my father, and very nearly outlived me.

thought: warns the museum not to lose it again
line: The museum will never lose it again, I trust. They had better not.

thought: the stranger looks useful; royal approval, briskly given
line: You have the look of someone useful, citizen. Do carry on.

thought: someone standing properly in his presence, for once
line: A citizen who stands up straight before his king. How refreshing.

thought: service is its own reward; he means it as praise
line: Serving your king is reward enough, and you look the serving sort.

thought: grudging assessment that the realm has good people
line: Misthalin is fortunate in some of its citizens. Possibly in you.

thought: no mud tramped in; the queen would approve
line: Good heavens, you wiped your feet. The queen will be delighted.

thought: measures by his father, who liked obedient people
line: My father would have liked the look of you. He liked a good listener.

thought: a royal nod is a gift; he says so
line: You may tell people the King nodded at you, citizen. I have, just now.

thought: points the stranger out to his advisor
line: Aeonisig, look, someone with a sense of purpose. Do make a note.

thought: the stranger hovering about the throne room
line: Are you lost, citizen, or merely loitering in a royal manner?

thought: every adventurer wants a reward; he offers the moral kind
line: A reward? Knowing you have helped your king is ample, citizen.

thought: yet another adventurer wanting something from the crown
line: Another adventurer wanting something from the crown. How novel.

thought: he has a realm to govern; the stranger plainly doesn't
line: Forgive me, citizen, but some of us have a realm to govern.

thought: mud on his palace floor and a likely culprit
line: Mud on the palace floor again, and one can guess whose boots.

thought: stares at the king like a tourist; must be new here
line: You must be new to palaces, citizen. One does not gawp at the King.

thought: suggests the silver be counted, to his advisor
line: Aeonisig, have the silver counted once this one has gone.

thought: expects a bow, gets a poor one, gives up
line: Bow, citizen, it is customary... no, lower. Oh, never mind.

thought: the petitions never stop; he wants it known how hard kingship is
line: Petitions, and more petitions. A crown is heavier than it looks.

thought: anticipates his stern advisor having opinions
line: Aeonisig will want a word about this, I expect. He always does.

thought: the queen runs him; he has made his peace with it
line: The queen has views on the curtains. I have learned to share them.

thought: has heard the grumbling about him and pretends not to mind
line: Some of my subjects say I am not much of a king. Quietly, I trust.

thought: proud of rebuilding Edgeville, sore nobody thanks him
line: I rebuilt Edgeville from a ruin, citizen. Nobody ever thanks a king.

thought: pious certainty about his kingdom and the river
line: This is Saradomin's kingdom, citizen. The blessed Salve keeps it so.

thought: Reldo taught him; he claims to read a lot, with a catch
line: Reldo taught me my letters. I read a great deal, when time allows.

thought: approves of Rovin's loyalty to him alone
line: Captain Rovin takes orders from nobody but his king. Quite right too.

thought: the stranger looks like they find things; things go missing here
line: You look like someone who finds things, citizen. Things go missing.

thought: an honest face, in a city of museum thieves
line: An honest face. Rare, in a city where gangs rob the museum.

thought: his father would have set this one after the shield
line: A capable sort! My father would have had you hunting that shield.

thought: looks bookish; Reldo would like that
line: You have a reader's look about you, citizen. Reldo would approve.

thought: points out a sensible face to Aeonisig, hopes it's no gang member
line: Aeonisig, there is a sensible face. Not in any gang, one trusts.

thought: steady hands, the sort that might bring back what was stolen
line: Steady hands, citizen. The sort that might bring back what was stolen.

thought: an adventurer who isn't asking him for money
line: Good heavens, an adventurer not asking me for money. How pleasant.

thought: condescending hope that this one might claim it
line: You might yet earn my father's reward, citizen. Stranger things have.

thought: the stranger looks lost; so is the shield, which matters more
line: Lost, citizen? So is Arrav's shield, and that is worth finding.

thought: nobody gets paid for standing about
line: There is a reward for that shield, citizen, not for standing about.

thought: doubts this one would spot a thief
line: You would not know the Phoenix Gang if they took your boots, I expect.

thought: so many adventurers, still no shield
line: So many adventurers in Varrock, and still no shield.

thought: looks at the stranger and resigns himself to waiting
line: My father waited his whole reign for that shield. I see I shall too.

thought: asks Aeonisig to agree this is no shield-finder
line: Aeonisig, does that one look like a shield-finder? Nor to me.

thought: gawping at the king earns nothing
line: One does not claim a king's reward by gawping at the king, citizen.

thought: dismissal dressed as politeness
line: Do not let me keep you, citizen. Clearly you have nothing to do.

thought: his father's reward still unclaimed
line: My father offered a fine reward for that shield. It stands still.

thought: indignant that thieves have kept the shield in his own city
line: A gang of thieves has had Arrav's shield for years. In my capital!

thought: a reward older than his reign bothers his sense of order
line: A reward that outlives the king who offered it. Most irregular.

thought: there's a history of it in his own library; he hasn't read it
line: My library has a whole book on that shield. I have not read it.

thought: dreads having to actually pay one day
line: Somebody will claim my father's reward one day. Then I must pay it.

thought: sniffs at the gang's grand name
line: The Phoenix Gang. Such a grand name for a pack of museum thieves.

thought: can't imagine what thieves do with a shield
line: Heaven knows what a gang wants with a shield. To hang over the fire?

thought: has heard the curator is still hunting
line: The curator is still searching for it, I am told. Bless the man.

thought: the stranger looks thoughtful, maybe a reader
line: A reader, I'd wager. You've a thoughtful sort of face, stranger.

thought: he loves to share what he knows
line: If ever you want to know anything, stranger, I'm happy to share.

thought: likens them to the old heroes, then a dry correction
line: You've the build of one of the old heroes... a little shorter.

thought: spots interest in history from the doorway
line: Interested in history? I could tell from the door, you know.

thought: thinks his wise friend would enjoy this one
line: Now there's someone who'd enjoy the Wise Old Man's company.

thought: they wiped their boots; the books are grateful
line: You wiped your boots! The books thank you, stranger.

thought: careful hands bring books back whole
line: Careful hands, I see. The sort that bring a book back in one piece.

thought: a keener pupil than the king was
line: If only the king had been as keen a pupil as you look, stranger.

thought: suspects they've never read a book; gently hopeful
line: Never opened a book in your life, have you? It's never too late.

thought: adventurers swing things near shelves
line: Do mind the shelves, stranger. Adventurers do tend to swing things.

thought: would lend a book but wants it back
line: I'd lend you a book, stranger, but I'd like it back, you see.

thought: reading is safe to try
line: Reading isn't catching, you know. You could try it quite safely.

thought: guesses they'd be a harder pupil than the king
line: You'd have been a harder pupil than the king, and he was hard.

thought: adventurers only come in for directions
line: Adventurers only come in here to ask the way out. Every one of them.

thought: another one walks past the library door
line: There goes another one past the library door. Not even a glance.

thought: recommends a book suited to them
line: I think you'd enjoy a book, you know. Something short, with pictures.

thought: hunting the goblin book he filed somewhere west
line: Now where did I file the goblin tribes? West end... I'm sure of it.

thought: Postie Pete will want his ordered books
line: Postie Pete will be in for his books, and I'll have to find them.

thought: he'd read here unpaid; a dry joke about the king
line: I'd read in here even if they didn't pay me. Don't tell the king.

thought: the census stops at the city's beginnings
line: The census goes back to the first camp. Before that... nothing.

thought: a stray fact about the Imcando and pie
line: The Imcando dwarves loved redberry pie. History's full of pie.

thought: books come back late, or not at all
line: People borrow books and return pressed flowers. Not the books, mind.

thought: folk tales stretch, but rest on something
line: A folk tale grows in the telling, but something's usually under it.

thought: recalling what the histories say of Robert the Strong
line: Robert the Strong fought dragonkin with a longbow, the histories say.

thought: a sharp look; likes puzzles, he guesses
line: There's a sharp look about you, stranger. Fond of a puzzle, I'd guess.

thought: someone who notices; Arrav would approve
line: Ah, someone who notices things! Arrav would have liked you.

thought: patience in a reader, rarer than courage
line: You've a reader's patience about you. That's rarer than courage.

thought: if anyone could find the shield
line: If anyone could find that old shield, I'd put my coin on you.

thought: curious people make history
line: Curious sort, aren't you? The best histories start with one of those.

thought: would lend the shield book to an honest face
line: I'd lend you the shield history, stranger. You've an honest face.

thought: reminded of heroes in his books, the short ones
line: You put me in mind of the old heroes in my books. The shorter ones.

thought: a thoughtful face is rare past the library
line: A thoughtful face. One sees so few of those come past the library.

thought: they'd walk past a famous shield
line: You'd walk straight past a famous stolen shield, I expect. Most do.

thought: they haven't read the shield history
line: You haven't read the history of the shield, have you? I thought not.

thought: heroes in the histories did read
line: History's full of heroes, stranger. Very few walked past libraries.

thought: they'd lose a shield quicker than the museum
line: You look like you'd lose a shield faster than the museum did.

thought: adventurers ask for treasure, not history
line: Adventurers ask me where the treasure is. Never what the history is.

thought: they don't know Arrav; there's a book
line: Do you know who Arrav was? Ah. Well, there's a book.

thought: fears they'd lose the shield if told
line: I'd tell you about the shield, but I fear you'd only go and lose it.

thought: someone using the library as shelter
line: Another one who thinks a library's for standing out of the rain.

thought: can't find the shield history again
line: That history of the shield... now which shelf did I give it?

thought: admires the gang's nerve, academically
line: The Phoenix Gang stole that shield from the museum. Bold, really.

thought: the Black Arm split, as gangs do
line: Then the Black Arm lot split from the Phoenix... gangs are like that.

thought: nobody has looked properly
line: Arrav's shield, gone all these years, and nobody's thought to look.

thought: the museum never got it back
line: The museum never did get that shield back, you know. Shocking, really.

thought: a history of thieves in a palace library amuses him
line: A history of thieves, kept in a palace. There's a joke in that.

thought: the story beats fiction
line: A stolen shield and a gang split in two. Better than most romances.

thought: Arrav's fame, which he agrees with
line: They say Arrav was the best-known hero of his age. I'd say so, too.

thought: asks after the hunt, hopeful
line: How goes the hunt, stranger? I've a good feeling about you.

thought: has heard they're asking about the shield
line: You've been asking about the shield, I hear. Splendid!

thought: brave to chase gangs for history
line: Brave of you, poking about after gangs for the sake of history.

thought: wants every word when they find it
line: If you do find the shield, stranger, I'll want to hear every word.

thought: promises a footnote, a scholar's honour
line: Ah, the shield-hunter. You'll be a footnote in the histories, surely.

thought: guesses they've been to Baraek
line: Been to see Baraek, have you? Good. Most people only buy furs.

thought: a reader who also does things
line: A reader and a doer. A rare combination, and a welcome one.

thought: worried for them in the south-west
line: Careful in the south-west, stranger. I'd hate to lose my best reader.

thought: the search is slow; years already
line: Still looking for that shield? It's been gone years. Take your time.

thought: too lost-looking for a gang
line: The Phoenix Gang won't take you on if you look that lost, I fear.

thought: asking a trader about gangs without buying
line: Asking Baraek about gangs? I'd have bought a fur first, to be polite.

thought: they're looking in the library for a shield
line: Shields don't turn up in libraries, stranger. I did check.

thought: can't imagine them in a gang
line: You, in a gang? I can't picture it, and I've a fine imagination.

thought: histories might mention them, in small print
line: If the histories ever mention you, it'll be in very small print.

thought: back for directions again
line: Back for directions again. The south-west is that way. Roughly.

thought: the search could fill its own volume
line: At this rate the shield history will need a second volume.

thought: surprised at what he heard about Baraek
line: Baraek and the Phoenix Gang, I heard. A fur trader! Who'd think it?

thought: Black Arm in the south-west; he stays put
line: The Black Arm keep to the south-west, they say. I keep to my books.

thought: wants the story to have an ending
line: I do hope that shield turns up. The history needs a last chapter.

thought: worries he gave poor directions
line: Did I send them to the right fur stall? There's only one, I believe.

thought: gangs everywhere, him among books
line: Gangs in the square, gangs in the south-west... and me with my books.

thought: the museum would want a new room
line: If the shield comes back, the museum will want a new room for it.

thought: the history is out, or misfiled
line: The shield history's out on loan. Or behind the goblin tribes.

thought: a librarian trading gang rumours
line: Gang rumours, from a librarian. The king would be shocked. Mildly.

thought: they look heroic; he wants that
line: Golly, you look like a proper hero, my friend! I want to be one too.

thought: offers a flower then remembers they're spoken for
line: Have a flower! No, wait, they're for... somebody. Have a sniff, then.

thought: kind face; would confide if he could remember
line: Kind face! I'd tell you my troubles if I could remember them.

thought: says they're lovely, as he does to all
line: You're lovely! Sorry, I say that to everyone, but you are!

thought: thinks he knows them
line: Oh, it's you! At least I think it's you. Hello anyway, my friend!

thought: they'd suit flowers
line: You'd look smashing with a bunch of flowers, my friend.

thought: would copy them if he became a hero
line: If I ever become a hero, I'll copy you exactly, my friend.

thought: someone nice in a grumpy city
line: Wooooo! Someone nice! Varrock's full of grumpy people.

thought: mistook them for someone important
line: From behind I thought you were someone important. Sorry, my friend!

thought: they look battered, like balcony victims
line: Did something fall on you off a balcony? Things do, you know.

thought: they look summons-prone, like him
line: You look the sort who gets court summonses. I get them too!

thought: they look tired, as from sermons
line: Golly, you look tired. Father Lawrence's sermons do that to people.

thought: neither will be heroes; solidarity
line: You'd never be a hero, would you? Me neither! Shake hands?

thought: a forgettable face, though he forgets all
line: Have we met? You've a very forgettable face. Not that I remember any.

thought: this one looks as lost as he is
line: Looks as lost as I am, that one. That's quite lost.

thought: nobody says hello first except him
line: Nobody in Varrock ever says hello first. Except me. And not this one.

thought: muddles the priest's name again
line: Lather... no. Father Lawrence. Why do I always get that one wrong?

thought: wandering, forgets where to
line: The square, then the general store, then... where was I going?

thought: flowers for someone he can't recall
line: These flowers were for somebody. Lovely somebody. Ermmm...

thought: a message is always a summons
line: A message? No, a court summons. They always are.

thought: wants to be a hero; heroes should get flowers
line: I always wanted to be a hero. Do heroes get flowers? They should.

thought: slept through the sermons
line: Father Lawrence's sermons... I slept through the last two, I think.

thought: thinks he went to school with Lawrence
line: I went to school with Father Lawrence. Or someone very like him.

thought: talks first to a stranger
line: Hello! You won't mind if I talk at you a bit? Nobody else stops.

thought: a messenger's face
line: You've the face of someone who carries messages. A good face!

thought: brave enough to face a father
line: Golly, you look brave! Brave enough to talk to a lady's father, even.

thought: they'd understand love, he thinks
line: You'd understand love, I can tell. Do you? I can't tell, actually.

thought: nearly as lovely as Juliet
line: You're nearly as lovely as Juliet! Not quite. Close, though.

thought: Juliet likes everyone but him
line: Juliet would like you. She likes everyone. Except me, some days.

thought: a friend; friends help with things
line: A friend! I need friends. Friends help with... ermmm... things.

thought: they walk like a hero; he walks like a florist
line: That one walks like a hero. I walk like a man carrying flowers.

thought: lucky in love, unlike him
line: You've a lucky look about you, my friend. Lucky in love, I bet.

thought: disappointed they're not Juliet
line: Oh. You're not Juliet. Never mind, you're still... somebody.

thought: fears they're the father
line: Are you her father? You're not, are you? You look cross enough.

thought: Juliet would throw things at them too
line: Golly, if Juliet saw that one she'd throw something.

thought: they look lonely, less than him
line: Lonely, are you, my friend? Not as lonely as me, but lonely.

thought: neither could climb a balcony
line: You'd never get up a balcony. Neither could I. We're alike!

thought: not much help, nor is he
line: Not much help, are you? Never mind. Nor am I.

thought: they look like a summons
line: You look like a court summons, my friend. Official and frightening.

thought: nobody's in love but him
line: Nobody's in love round here except me. Not even that one.

thought: unsure of her name
line: Her name's Juliet, I'm almost sure. It begins with a J, anyway.

thought: her father forbids them; can't recall him
line: Her father won't let us meet. Her father! Whoever he is.

thought: she's in the west; he's been there once
line: She lives on the west side of the city. I've been there! Once.

thought: would sing again but she throws things
line: I'd sing up to her balcony again, but she throws things.

thought: wishes for a messenger
line: If only someone would carry her a message. A nice one, not a summons.

thought: waiting in the square for love
line: I'll wait in the square. Love waits in squares, I think.

thought: flowers will come back at him
line: Flowers for Juliet again. She'll throw them back. She's a good arm.

thought: heart west, feet in the square
line: My heart's in the west of the city and my feet are in the square.

thought: they're helping him, he thinks
line: You're helping me, aren't you? Golly! I think you are!

thought: his messenger; forgot the name
line: My dearest, bravest messenger! What was your name again?

thought: they'd walk past her father
line: You're braver than me. You'd walk right past her father!

thought: they might make him a hero
line: If I ever become a hero, it'll be your fault. In a good way!

thought: back, or new; either way wonderful
line: Wooooo! You came back! Or you're new. Either way, wonderful!

thought: they don't look like a father
line: You've not got a face like a father. That's the nicest thing I know.

thought: muddles friend and love
line: There goes a friend in love. A friend to love. A friend, anyway.

thought: Juliet's lucky to have them both
line: Juliet's lucky to have us. Well, me. And you, for the moment.

thought: a stern look; might be the father
line: Wait, are you her father? You're not? Then why the stern look?

thought: someone is late; unsure who
line: You took your time! Or I did. One of us is late, my friend.

thought: they look grim; wants good news
line: Golly, you look grim. Bring good news next time, not that face.

thought: a slow messenger
line: You don't run very fast for a messenger, do you, my friend?

thought: wants nothing to do with potions
line: Potions and I don't agree. Somebody else can drink that sort of thing.

thought: they look like a father; stand off
line: You look a bit like a father. Any father. Do stand further off.

thought: they forgot the message, as he would
line: Did you forget the message? I'd forget the message. We're so alike!

thought: unsure whose side this one is on
line: Is that one on my side or her father's? Hard to say. Shifty.

thought: any man could be her father
line: Every man in Varrock could be her father. Every single one!

thought: spots a man, panics, decides baker
line: Is that him? Is that her father? No... a baker. Probably.

thought: sworn to be killed by someone unknown
line: Her father's sworn to kill me. I'd hide, if I knew who from.

thought: didn't follow the potion plan
line: A potion to make her look... ermmm. I didn't follow that bit.

thought: keeping out of the west side
line: I'm keeping out of sight. Well, out of the west side. Mostly.

thought: a disguise he'd forget
line: Should I wear a disguise? I'd only forget I was wearing it.

thought: hid from a stern man behind flowers
line: A stern-looking man went by, so I hid behind my flowers. Golly.

thought: fathers make love hard
line: Love's easy. It's the fathers that make it hard.
